3.3 — Train One Epoch¶

Objective: Implement a reusable training function that updates the MLP's weights and biases through forward propagation, loss computation, backpropagation, and SGD optimization.

Procedure:

  1. Set training mode: Call model.train() to put the model in training mode.

  2. Iterate through training batches: Use the training DataLoader to retrieve batches of normalized BloodMNIST images and their corresponding labels.

  3. Prepare batch tensors:

    • Move images and labels to the same computation device as the model.
    • Convert labels from [B, 1] to [B] when necessary.
    • Ensure labels have the integer data type required by CrossEntropyLoss.

  4. Reset gradients: Call optimizer.zero_grad() to clear gradients from the previous batch.

  5. Forward propagation: Pass the images through the MLP to obtain logits of shape [B, 8].

  6. Calculate loss: Use CrossEntropyLoss to compare the predicted logits with the ground-truth labels.

  7. Backward propagation: Call loss.backward() to calculate gradients for all trainable model parameters.

  8. Update parameters: Call optimizer.step() to update weights and biases using SGD.

  9. Track training loss: Accumulate batch losses weighted by the number of samples and calculate the mean training loss over the processed samples.

  10. Return training loss: Return the average training loss for monitoring and comparison.

Expected Result:

  • Each processed training batch performs one forward pass, backward pass, and optimizer update.
  • The model's trainable parameters are updated.
  • The function returns a single scalar representing the average training loss.

Purpose: Establish a reusable training loop for the D2, D5, D10, and D20 models and for the activation-function experiments in Stage B.

Important Notes:

  • loss.backward() computes gradients but does not update parameters.
  • optimizer.step() updates parameters using the computed gradients.
  • Gradients must be cleared before processing each new batch.
  • The optional max_batches argument limits the number of batches for debugging. By default, the function processes the complete training DataLoader.
  • Layer-wise gradient recording will be added in Part 4, after loss.backward() and before optimizer.step().
In [ ]:
# Train the model for one epoch (or a limited number of batches for debugging)
def train_one_epoch(model, loader, criterion, optimizer, device, max_batches=None):

    model.train()            # Enable training mode; model parameters can be updated
    total_loss = 0.0         # Accumulate sample-weighted batch losses
    total_samples = 0        # Count the samples actually processed

    # Process mini-batches from the training DataLoader
    for batch_idx, (images, labels) in enumerate(loader):

        if max_batches is not None and batch_idx >= max_batches:
            break           # Stop early for debugging; None means all batches

        images = images.to(device)                     # Images: [B, 3, 28, 28], on model's device
        labels = labels.squeeze(-1).long().to(device)  # Labels: [B, 1] -> [B], int64 for CrossEntropyLoss

        # Forward pass, loss calculation, and backpropagation
        optimizer.zero_grad()              # Clear gradients left from the previous batch
        logits = model(images)             # Forward: [B, 3, 28, 28] -> [B, 8]
        loss = criterion(logits, labels)   # Mean CrossEntropyLoss for the current batch

        if not torch.isfinite(loss).item():
            raise ValueError("Training loss is NaN or infinite")

        loss.backward()                    # Compute gradients dLoss/dWeight and dLoss/dBias
        optimizer.step()                   # Update parameters using SGD and the computed gradients

        # Track mean training loss, accounting for different batch sizes
        batch_size = images.size(0)        # Number of images in the current batch
        total_loss += loss.item() * batch_size  # Convert mean batch loss to summed sample loss
        total_samples += batch_size        # Include each processed image in the denominator

    if total_samples == 0:
        raise ValueError("No training samples were processed")

    epoch_loss = total_loss / total_samples  # Average loss per processed training image

    return epoch_loss

3.4 — Evaluate Model on the Validation Set¶

Objective: Implement a reusable evaluation function to measure classification performance on the BloodMNIST validation dataset without updating model parameters.

Procedure:

  1. Set evaluation mode: Call model.eval() to switch the model to evaluation mode.

  2. Disable gradient tracking: Use torch.no_grad() to avoid constructing unnecessary computational graphs during validation.

  3. Process validation batches: Iterate through val_loader, moving images and labels to the model's computation device.

  4. Forward propagation: Pass validation images through the model to obtain raw logits of shape [B, 8].

  5. Calculate validation loss: Use the same CrossEntropyLoss function as training, without backward propagation.

  6. Generate predictions: Use argmax(dim=1) to select the class with the highest logit for each image.

  7. Accumulate results: Collect the true labels and predicted labels across the entire validation dataset.

  8. Calculate validation metrics:

    • Validation loss: Average CrossEntropyLoss per validation image.
    • Validation accuracy: Proportion of correctly classified images.
    • Validation macro-F1: Unweighted average of F1 scores across all 8 classes.

  9. Return metrics: Return a dictionary containing validation loss, accuracy, and macro-F1.

Expected Result:

A dictionary containing:

  • loss: Scalar validation loss.
  • accuracy: Classification accuracy between 0 and 1.
  • macro_f1: Macro-averaged F1 score between 0 and 1.

Purpose: Evaluate and compare model performance on the same held-out validation split across different network depths and activation functions.

Important Notes:

  • Validation does not call loss.backward() or optimizer.step().
  • Validation uses the official BloodMNIST validation split, not the test split.
  • Macro-F1 is calculated using predictions from the complete validation set, rather than averaging individual batch F1 scores.
  • All 8 classes are included when calculating macro-F1, even if a class has no predictions.
  • The same evaluation function and metric definitions will be used for all experimental conditions.
In [32]:
# Evaluate classification performance without updating model parameters
def evaluate(model, loader, criterion, device, num_classes):

    model.eval()             # Evaluation mode; no parameter updates in this function
    total_loss = 0.0         # Accumulate sample-weighted validation losses
    total_correct = 0        # Count correctly classified images
    total_samples = 0        # Count all validation images

    all_labels = []          # Ground-truth labels collected across batches
    all_predictions = []     # Predicted labels collected across batches

    # Run inference without building computational graphs
    with torch.no_grad():

        for images, labels in loader:

            images = images.to(device)                     # Validation images: [B, 3, 28, 28]
            labels = labels.squeeze(-1).long().to(device)  # Labels: [B, 1] -> [B]

            # Calculate validation loss and predicted classes
            logits = model(images)             # Forward pass: [B, 8] raw logits
            loss = criterion(logits, labels)   # Mean CrossEntropyLoss for this batch
            predictions = logits.argmax(dim=1)  # Highest-logit class index for each image: [B]

            # Accumulate loss and accuracy statistics
            batch_size = images.size(0)        # Number of images in this validation batch
            total_loss += loss.item() * batch_size  # Sample-weighted loss accumulation
            total_correct += (predictions == labels).sum().item()  # Number of correct predictions
            total_samples += batch_size        # Total validation images processed so far

            # Store labels and predictions for dataset-level macro-F1
            all_labels.extend(labels.cpu().tolist())            # Move true labels to CPU as Python values
            all_predictions.extend(predictions.cpu().tolist())  # Move predicted labels to CPU

    if total_samples == 0:
        raise ValueError("No validation samples were processed")

    # Calculate metrics over the complete validation dataset
    val_loss = total_loss / total_samples       # Mean validation loss per image
    val_accuracy = total_correct / total_samples  # Fraction of correctly classified images

    val_macro_f1 = f1_score(
        all_labels,                             # Ground-truth classes
        all_predictions,                        # Predicted classes
        labels=list(range(num_classes)),        # Include all 8 BloodMNIST classes
        average="macro",                        # Unweighted mean of per-class F1 scores
        zero_division=0                         # Assign F1=0 when undefined
    )

    # Return all validation metrics in a dictionary
    return {
        "loss": val_loss,
        "accuracy": val_accuracy,
        "macro_f1": val_macro_f1
    }

3.5 — Short D2 Training Trial¶

Objective: Perform a short training and validation trial using the baseline D2 model to verify that the training pipeline operates correctly before implementing gradient measurements and running the main experiments.

Procedure:

  1. Use the freshly initialized D2 model and SGD optimizer created in Section 3.2.

  2. Set a small debugging budget:

    • debug_epochs = 2
    • debug_batches = 5 training batches per epoch.

  3. Train D2: Call train_one_epoch() to perform forward propagation, calculate CrossEntropyLoss, compute gradients, and update parameters using SGD.

  4. Evaluate D2: After each training epoch, call evaluate() on the complete validation set to calculate:

    • Validation loss.
    • Validation accuracy.
    • Validation macro-F1.

  5. Check numerical stability: Verify that the training loss and validation metrics are finite (no NaN or infinity).

  6. Display results: Print training loss, validation loss, validation accuracy, and validation macro-F1 after each epoch.

Expected Result:

  • The training and validation functions execute without errors.
  • Forward propagation, backpropagation, and optimizer updates run successfully.
  • Training and validation losses are finite.
  • Validation accuracy and macro-F1 can be calculated.
  • The model's training parameters can be updated.

Purpose: Detect errors in the integration of the data pipeline, MLP architecture, loss function, optimizer, and validation function before adding gradient measurements.

Important Notes:

  • This is a debugging trial, not a final research experiment.
  • Only a small number of training batches are processed per epoch.
  • The full validation set is used for evaluation.
  • Validation metrics from this trial must not be interpreted as final model performance.
  • The learning rate is provisional and will be assessed in the Part 5 learning-rate sanity pilot.
  • Fresh models and controlled DataLoaders will be used for subsequent experimental runs.

# Run a short D2 training trial to verify the training and validation pipeline
debug_epochs = 2                 # Run only 2 epochs for this initial debugging test
debug_batches = 5                # Process only 5 training batches per epoch

for epoch in range(1, debug_epochs + 1):

    # Train D2 on a small number of batches
    train_loss = train_one_epoch(
        model=model_d2_train,     # Fresh D2 model created in Section 3.2
        loader=train_loader,      # Normalized BloodMNIST training batches
        criterion=criterion,      # CrossEntropyLoss from Section 3.1
        optimizer=optimizer,      # SGD updates weights and biases after each batch
        device=device,            # Same device used for model and tensors
        max_batches=debug_batches # Limit training to 5 batches for debugging
    )

    val_metrics = evaluate(
        model=model_d2_train,     # Evaluate the model after this epoch's updates
        loader=val_loader,        # Official BloodMNIST validation split

        device=device,
        num_classes=cfg.num_classes
    )

        f"Epoch {epoch}/{debug_epochs} | "
        f"Train Loss: {train_loss:.4f} | "
        f"Val Loss: {val_metrics['loss']:.4f} | "
        f"Val Accuracy: {val_metrics['accuracy']:.4f} | "
        f"Val Macro-F1: {val_metrics['macro_f1']:.4f}"
    )

Part 4 — Gradient & Trainability Measurements¶

1. Overview & Objective¶

Part 4 implements the measurement system used to investigate gradient attenuation and early-layer trainability in the BloodMNIST MLP experiments.

Building on the training pipeline in Part 3, this part introduces two primary measurements:

  1. Layer-wise RMS weight-gradient magnitude: Quantifies the magnitude of weight gradients at each hidden Linear layer.
  2. Normalized first-layer weight displacement: Quantifies how far the first hidden layer's weights have moved from their initial values.

These measurements support H1 (depth-dependent gradient attenuation) and H2 (the association between gradient attenuation and early-layer trainability). The same measurement protocol is also reused in Stage B to compare activation functions.

2. Measurement Definitions¶

2.1 Layer-Wise RMS Weight Gradients¶

For hidden Linear layer (\ell), with (N_\ell) weight parameters, the RMS weight-gradient magnitude is:

$$ \boxed{ G_\ell = \sqrt{ \frac{1}{N_\ell} \sum_{i=1}^{N_\ell} \left(\frac{\partial L}{\partial W_{\ell,i}}\right)^2 } } $$

where:

  • $L$ is the current mini-batch CrossEntropyLoss.
  • $W_{\ell,i}$ is the $i$-th weight parameter of hidden layer (\ell).
  • $N_\ell$ is the number of weights in that layer.

RMS accounts for differences in parameter counts and provides a comparable measure of gradient magnitude per weight element.

Measurements use layer.weight.grad after backpropagation. Bias gradients and the output layer are excluded from the primary layer-wise analysis.

For relative comparisons, the first-to-last hidden-layer gradient ratio is calculated from the recorded RMS measurements:

$$ \boxed{ R = \frac{G_{\mathrm{first}}}{G_{\mathrm{last}}} } $$

A smaller ratio indicates stronger relative attenuation of first-layer weight gradients under the measured conditions.

Measurement distinction: RMS weight gradients are not identical to gradients of the loss with respect to hidden activations or to the network's Jacobian matrices.

2.2 Normalized First-Layer Weight Displacement¶

To measure early-layer weight movement, the initial first-layer weight matrix is saved before training.

At the end of epoch $e$, normalized first-layer weight displacement is calculated as:

$$ \boxed{ D_1(e) = \frac{\left\|W_1(e)-W_1(0)\right\|_F} {\left\|W_1(0)\right\|_F} } $$

where:

  • $W_1(0)$ is the first hidden layer's initial weight matrix.
  • $W_1(e)$ is its weight matrix after epoch (e).
  • $\|\cdot\|_F$ denotes the Frobenius norm.

This metric measures the net displacement from initialization, normalized by the initial weight magnitude. It is not the sum of individual SGD update magnitudes or the percentage of weight parameters that changed.

Under the plain SGD protocol defined in Part 3, the measurements help examine whether smaller early-layer gradients are associated with smaller weight displacement and slower training-loss reduction.

3. Gradient Recording Protocol¶

The GradientRecorder class introduced in Section 4.3 implements a consistent measurement schedule across experimental runs.

Measurement Recording Frequency Purpose
Early-step RMS gradients Every optimizer step during the first 100 global training steps Inspect gradient behavior at the beginning of training.
Epoch-level RMS gradients First 10 training batches of every epoch Track layer-wise gradient evolution throughout training.
First-layer weight displacement At the end of every epoch Measure early-layer weight movement over time.

For epoch (e) and hidden layer (\ell), the mean RMS gradient is:

$$ \overline{G}_{\ell,e} = \frac{1}{10} \sum_{b=1}^{10}G_{\ell,e,b} $$

where $G_{\ell,e,b}$ is the gradient RMS recorded for sampled batch (b).

The first-100-step and first-10-batches-per-epoch windows may overlap. A batch belonging to both windows is measured once and its value is reused without duplicate counting within an epoch-level average.

The global step counter continues across epochs within a training run. All main experimental conditions use the same recording rules.

Important distinction: Epoch-level RMS values summarize ten sampled batches, not the gradient magnitude averaged over every batch in the epoch.

4. Measurement Integration & Recorded Outputs¶

Section 4.4 extends the train_one_epoch() function defined in Part 3 with an optional GradientRecorder.

The measurement-integrated training sequence is:

Training batch → Forward pass → CrossEntropyLoss → Backward pass → Record gradients → SGD update

Gradient RMS values are recorded after loss.backward() and before optimizer.step(), so they represent the gradients used for the current SGD update.

At the end of the epoch, the recorder calculates first-layer weight displacement using the updated parameters.

Output Contents Used For
step_records Global step, epoch, hidden-layer index, RMS gradient Early-training gradient analysis
epoch_mean_records() Epoch, hidden layer, mean sampled RMS, batch count Gradient evolution across epochs
weight_change_records Epoch, normalized first-layer weight displacement Early-layer trainability analysis

The recorder observes and stores measurements without changing the underlying SGD update rule. When recorder=None, training proceeds without measurement logging.

5. Workflow & Section Guide¶

Section Main Task Research Role
4.1 — RMS Gradient Functions Implement safe_l2_norm() and gradient_rms(). Measure hidden-layer weight-gradient magnitudes.
4.2 — First-Layer Weight Change Implement first_layer_weight_change(). Measure normalized displacement from initial weights.
4.3 — Gradient Recorder Define GradientRecorder and its recording schedule. Collect measurements consistently across steps and epochs.
4.4 — Training Integration Extend train_one_epoch() with optional gradient recording. Record measurements during normal SGD training.
4.5 — Single-Batch Verification Test gradients and weight changes on a fresh D2 model. Verify basic numerical validity and layer indexing.
4.6 — Multi-Batch Verification Check logging across two 12-batch D2 debugging passes. Verify step tracking, epoch summaries, and recording counts.

Sections 4.5–4.6 are implementation checks, not main experimental runs. The complete recording protocol is subsequently verified through the integrated training pipeline in Part 5.

6. Connections to Subsequent Parts¶

  • Part 5 — Pipeline Verification & Pilot: Integrates the recorder with run_training(), checks measurement completeness, and finalizes the experimental protocol.
  • Part 6 — Stage A: Compares layer-wise RMS gradients, gradient evolution, and first-layer displacement across D2, D5, D10, and D20 under the Sigmoid baseline.
  • Part 7 — Stage B: Reuses the measurement system to compare Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU at fixed D5 depth.
  • Part 8 — Final Reporting: Summarizes recorded measurements across seeds and interprets their relationships with optimization and validation performance.

7. Expected Outcome & Role in the Experiment¶

Part 4 establishes reusable, verified measurement functions and a gradient recorder that can be applied consistently across experimental conditions.

Its primary contribution is to connect internal optimization measurements (weight gradients and early-layer displacement) with the training-loss and validation-performance metrics established in Part 3.

The recorded quantities support empirical comparisons of gradient attenuation and trainability; they do not independently establish a causal mechanism.

4.1 — Measure Layer-Wise RMS Gradients¶

Objective: Implement a reusable function to measure the root mean square (RMS) of weight gradients for individual hidden Linear layers.

Procedure:

  1. Access the weight-gradient tensor of a Linear layer through layer.weight.grad after loss.backward().

  2. Calculate the RMS gradient using:

    $$ \operatorname{RMS}(g)=\sqrt{\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}g_i^2} =\frac{\|g\|_2}{\sqrt{N}} $$

    where g contains all elements of the layer's weight-gradient matrix and N is the number of gradient elements.

  3. Use a numerically stable L2 norm calculation to reduce floating-point underflow when measuring very small gradients.

  4. Return one scalar RMS gradient value for each weight-gradient tensor.

  5. Apply the same calculation to every hidden Linear layer across all model depths and activation functions.

Expected Result:

  • D2 produces 2 hidden-layer RMS gradient values per recorded training step.
  • D5 produces 5 values.
  • D10 produces 10 values.
  • D20 produces 20 values.

Purpose: Quantify the magnitude of gradients reaching each hidden layer and investigate whether deeper networks exhibit stronger gradient attenuation near the input.

Important Notes:

  • RMS is preferred over raw L2 norm because it accounts for the number of weight parameters in each layer.
  • Gradients are measured only after backpropagation.
  • The main analysis focuses on weight gradients of hidden Linear layers, excluding biases and the output layer.
  • Very small or zero RMS values are possible and should not automatically be treated as implementation errors.
In [34]:
# Calculate a numerically stable L2 norm for tensors with potentially tiny values
def safe_l2_norm(tensor):

    values = tensor.detach()                  # Use tensor values without tracking gradients
    scale = values.abs().max()                # Find the largest absolute element to rescale the tensor

    if scale.item() == 0.0:
        return 0.0                            # A tensor containing only zeros has L2 norm = 0

    return (scale * (values / scale).norm()).item()  # ||g||₂ = scale × ||g / scale||₂


# Calculate RMS gradient per weight parameter
def gradient_rms(gradient):

    grad_norm = safe_l2_norm(gradient)        # L2 norm of the gradient tensor
    num_params = gradient.numel()             # Number of weight-gradient elements

    return grad_norm / (num_params ** 0.5)    # RMS(g) = ||g||₂ / sqrt(N)

4.2 — Measure Early-Layer Normalized Weight Change¶

Objective: Measure how much the first hidden layer's weights change relative to their initial values during training.

Procedure:

  1. Before training begins, save a detached copy of the first hidden layer's initial weight matrix, W₁(0).

  2. After training updates, retrieve the current weight matrix, W₁(t).

  3. Calculate the normalized weight change:

    $$ \operatorname{WeightChange}(t) =\frac{\|W_1(t)-W_1(0)\|_F} {\|W_1(0)\|_F} $$

  4. Calculate this metric at the end of each training epoch.

  5. Record the value for later comparisons across model depths, activations, and random seeds.

Expected Result:

  • Before training: Normalized weight change = 0.
  • After training: A nonnegative scalar representing the relative change in the first hidden layer's weights.
  • One recorded value per epoch for each model run.

Purpose: Evaluate early-layer trainability by examining whether conditions with smaller gradients also exhibit smaller cumulative weight changes.

This measurement supports the second research hypothesis (H2), which investigates the relationship between gradient attenuation, parameter updates, and learning progress.

Important Notes:

  • Only the first hidden layer is measured to keep the analysis focused.
  • The initial weight matrix must be saved before the first optimizer update.
  • Use .detach().clone() to preserve an independent snapshot of the original weights.
  • This metric measures cumulative displacement from initialization, not the magnitude of one individual SGD update.
  • A small weight change alone does not prove gradient vanishing; it must be interpreted alongside gradients and training-loss behavior.
In [35]:
# Measure how much the first hidden layer's weights have changed from initialization
def first_layer_weight_change(model, initial_weight):

    current_weight = model.linear_layers()[0].weight.detach()  # Current weights of Hidden Layer 1

    if current_weight.shape != initial_weight.shape:
        raise ValueError("Initial and current weights must have the same shape")

    initial_norm = safe_l2_norm(initial_weight)   # ||W₁(0)||₂, the reference weight magnitude

    if initial_norm == 0.0:
        raise ValueError("Initial weight norm must be nonzero")

    weight_difference = current_weight - initial_weight  # W₁(t) - W₁(0)

    change_norm = safe_l2_norm(weight_difference)  # ||W₁(t) - W₁(0)||₂

    return change_norm / initial_norm               # Relative weight change from initialization

4.3 — Define Gradient Recorder¶

Objective: Implement a reusable gradient recorder that tracks layer-wise RMS gradients during training and cumulative weight changes in the first hidden layer.

Recording Protocol:

  1. Early-step gradient logging: Record the RMS gradient of every hidden Linear layer at each of the first 100 optimizer steps.

  2. Epoch-level gradient logging: For every epoch, record gradients from the first 10 training batches and calculate the mean RMS gradient for each hidden layer.

  3. Early-layer weight change: Record the normalized weight change of Hidden Layer 1 at the end of every epoch.

  4. Consistent measurement rules: Apply the same recording protocol to all model depths, activations, and random seeds.

Procedure:

  1. Define a GradientRecorder class to manage gradient measurements and recorded results.

  2. Initialize the recorder with a model before training begins.

  3. Save an independent copy of the first hidden layer's initial weight matrix.

  4. Maintain a global optimizer-step counter across epochs.

  5. Define record() to measure hidden-layer RMS gradients after loss.backward() and before optimizer.step().

  6. Store early-step measurements for the first 100 training steps.

  7. Accumulate the RMS values from the first 10 training batches of each epoch.

  8. Define finish_epoch() to record the first hidden layer's normalized weight change after the epoch's optimizer updates.

  9. Define epoch_mean_records() to calculate the mean RMS gradient per hidden layer and epoch.

Expected Result:

The recorder provides three collections:

  • step_records: Layer-wise RMS gradients during the first 100 training steps.
  • epoch_mean_records(): Mean RMS gradients calculated from the first 10 batches of each epoch.
  • weight_change_records: Normalized first-hidden-layer weight changes measured at the end of each epoch.

Purpose: Collect consistent measurements for evaluating gradient attenuation, its evolution during training, and its relationship with early-layer trainability.

These measurements will later support the depth comparisons in Stage A and the activation-function comparisons in Stage B.

Important Notes:

  • The recorder is created separately for each experimental run.
  • The global step counter continues across epochs rather than restarting at each epoch.
  • Gradient measurements must occur after backward propagation and before optimizer updates.
  • Recording a gradient does not modify the gradient tensor or the model's parameters.
  • Only hidden-layer weight gradients are included in the primary gradient analysis.
  • The first 100 steps and first 10 batches per epoch are overlapping sampling windows; their measurements are not counted twice within the same summary.
In [36]:
# Record hidden-layer gradients and early-layer weight changes during training
class GradientRecorder:

    def __init__(self, model, first_steps=100, epoch_batches=10):

        # Set a fixed measurement protocol for every experimental run
        self.first_steps = first_steps               # Record every step during the first 100 optimizer steps
        self.epoch_batches = epoch_batches           # Use the first 10 batches of each epoch
        self.global_step = 0                         # Count optimizer steps continuously across epochs

        # Save initial weights before the first optimizer update
        self.initial_weight = model.linear_layers()[0].weight.detach().clone()  # Initial Hidden Layer 1 weights

        # Prepare containers for measurements collected during training
        self.step_records = []                       # Individual RMS values during the first 100 steps
        self.epoch_sums = {}                         # Sum of sampled RMS values for each (epoch, layer)
        self.epoch_counts = {}                       # Number of sampled batches for each (epoch, layer)
        self.weight_change_records = []              # Cumulative Hidden Layer 1 weight change per epoch

    # Record gradients immediately after backward propagation
    def record(self, model, epoch, batch_idx):

        self.global_step += 1                        # Advance the global step counter once per training batch

        record_step = self.global_step <= self.first_steps  # True during the first 100 steps
        record_epoch = batch_idx < self.epoch_batches       # True for batch indices 0 to 9 of each epoch

        if not (record_step or record_epoch):
            return                                   # Skip gradient measurements outside both sampling windows

        # Measure the weight-gradient RMS of each hidden Linear layer
        for layer_id, layer in enumerate(model.linear_layers()[:-1], start=1):

            grad = layer.weight.grad                 # Gradient computed by loss.backward() for this layer

            if grad is None:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Gradient missing at hidden layer {layer_id}")

            rms = gradient_rms(grad)                 # Compute one RMS scalar for the layer's weight gradients

            if not np.isfinite(rms):
                raise ValueError(f"Non-finite gradient RMS at hidden layer {layer_id}")

            # Keep one record per layer and step during the initial 100 steps
            if record_step:
                self.step_records.append({
                    "step": self.global_step,         # Global optimizer-step number (starts at 1)
                    "epoch": epoch,                   # Epoch during which the gradient was measured
                    "layer": layer_id,                # Hidden layer position, counted from the input
                    "grad_rms": rms                   # RMS gradient measured before the SGD update
                })

            # Accumulate the first 10 batch measurements for epoch-level averaging
            if record_epoch:
                key = (epoch, layer_id)               # Identify a particular epoch and hidden layer
                self.epoch_sums[key] = self.epoch_sums.get(key, 0.0) + rms
                self.epoch_counts[key] = self.epoch_counts.get(key, 0) + 1

    # Measure cumulative weight change after an epoch finishes
    def finish_epoch(self, model, epoch):

        change = first_layer_weight_change(model, self.initial_weight)  # Compare current W₁ with initial W₁

        self.weight_change_records.append({
            "epoch": epoch,
            "first_layer_weight_change": change
        })

    # Calculate one mean gradient RMS per hidden layer and epoch
    def epoch_mean_records(self):

        records = []

        for (epoch, layer_id), total in sorted(self.epoch_sums.items()):

            count = self.epoch_counts[(epoch, layer_id)]  # Number of sampled batches for this epoch/layer

            records.append({
                "epoch": epoch,
                "layer": layer_id,
                "mean_grad_rms": total / count,           # Arithmetic mean of sampled batch RMS values
                "batches": count                          # Normally 10 batches in a full training epoch
            })

        return records

4.4 — Integrate Gradient Recording into the Training Loop¶

Objective: Extend the existing train_one_epoch() function to collect gradient and early-layer weight-change measurements without changing the training procedure.

Procedure:

  1. Keep the original training steps:

    • Prepare mini-batches.
    • Reset gradients.
    • Perform forward propagation.
    • Calculate CrossEntropyLoss.
    • Perform backward propagation.
    • Update parameters using SGD.

  2. Add two optional function arguments:

    • recorder: A GradientRecorder object that collects measurements during training.
    • epoch: The current epoch number used to label the records.

  3. After loss.backward(), call recorder.record() before optimizer.step().

  4. At the end of the epoch, call recorder.finish_epoch() to measure the normalized weight change of Hidden Layer 1.

  5. Continue returning the average training loss as before.

Expected Result:

  • Training works normally when recorder=None.
  • When a recorder is provided, gradients are captured before SGD updates.
  • The recorder stores early-step RMS values, epoch-level RMS summaries, and early-layer weight changes.
  • The training function continues to return one scalar training loss.

Purpose: Integrate the measurement system into the existing reusable training pipeline while preserving the controlled SGD optimization protocol.

Required Order:

optimizer.zero_grad()
logits = model(images)
loss = criterion(logits, labels)
loss.backward()
recorder.record(model, epoch, batch_idx)
optimizer.step()

The recorder must not be placed before loss.backward() or after optimizer.step().

Important Notes:

  • The same training function will be used for all depths, activations, and random seeds.
  • No gradient clipping, momentum, weight decay, or adaptive optimizer is added by the recorder.
  • A new recorder must be created for each fresh experimental model before its first optimizer update.
  • The max_batches argument remains available for short debugging trials.
In [37]:
# Train one epoch, with optional gradient and weight-change recording
def train_one_epoch(model, loader, criterion, optimizer, device,
                    max_batches=None, recorder=None, epoch=None):

    if recorder is not None and epoch is None:
        raise ValueError("Pass epoch when using a gradient recorder")

    model.train()                 # Enable training mode before processing batches
    total_loss = 0.0              # Accumulate sample-weighted training losses
    total_samples = 0             # Count the training images processed in this epoch

    # Process training mini-batches
    for batch_idx, (images, labels) in enumerate(loader):

        if max_batches is not None and batch_idx >= max_batches:
            break                # Process all batches unless a debug limit is specified

        images = images.to(device)                     # Images: [B, 3, 28, 28] on the selected device
        labels = labels.reshape(-1).long().to(device)  # Labels: [B, 1] or [B] -> [B], dtype int64

        # Forward propagation and classification loss
        optimizer.zero_grad()              # Remove gradients accumulated from the previous batch
        logits = model(images)             # Forward: normalized images -> 8 logits per image
        loss = criterion(logits, labels)   # Mean CrossEntropyLoss for the current mini-batch

        if not torch.isfinite(loss).item():
            raise ValueError("Training loss is NaN or infinite")

        # Backpropagation, gradient recording, and SGD update
        loss.backward()                    # Calculate gradients of loss with respect to weights and biases

        if recorder is not None:
            recorder.record(
                model,                     # Model whose hidden-layer gradients are being measured
                epoch=epoch,               # Current training epoch
                batch_idx=batch_idx        # Zero-based batch position within the current epoch
            )

        optimizer.step()                   # Update parameters AFTER the gradient measurements

        # Calculate the sample-weighted training loss
        batch_size = images.size(0)        # Number of images in this mini-batch
        total_loss += loss.item() * batch_size  # Convert mean batch loss into summed sample loss
        total_samples += batch_size        # Track the number of processed images

    if total_samples == 0:
        raise ValueError("No training samples were processed")

    # Record cumulative first-layer weight change after all SGD updates in this epoch
    if recorder is not None:
        recorder.finish_epoch(model, epoch)

    epoch_loss = total_loss / total_samples  # Mean training loss over processed samples

    return epoch_loss

4.5 — Verify Gradient Recorder with the D2 Model¶

Objective: Verify that the gradient recorder correctly measures hidden-layer RMS gradients and first-layer weight changes using a single D2 training batch.

Procedure:

  1. Create a fresh baseline D2 model and move it to the configured device.

  2. Initialize a new GradientRecorder before the first optimizer update.

  3. Prepare a small batch of 8 normalized BloodMNIST training images and their corresponding labels.

  4. Create an SGD optimizer using the current experimental configuration.

  5. Perform one forward pass and calculate CrossEntropyLoss.

  6. Call loss.backward() to compute gradients for all trainable parameters.

  7. Before calling optimizer.step(), record and display RMS gradients for Hidden Layers 1 and 2.

  8. Verify that the gradient tensors exist and all recorded RMS values are finite.

  9. Measure the first hidden layer's normalized weight change before and after one SGD update.

Expected Result:

  • Two hidden-layer RMS gradient values are recorded.
  • Both gradient values are finite.
  • The normalized first-layer weight change equals zero before the update.
  • The first-layer weight change remains finite after the update.

Purpose: Confirm that gradient measurements are correctly integrated with backpropagation and can be used to study gradient propagation across model depth.

Important Notes:

  • This is a single-batch verification, not a full training experiment.
  • Gradient values may be very small, especially in deep networks.
  • A recorded gradient of zero must be distinguished from a missing gradient (grad is None).
  • Very small SGD updates may produce zero observable weight change due to floating-point precision.
  • The learning rate is provisional and will be assessed during the Part 5 learning-rate pilot.
In [38]:
# Create a fresh D2 model and recorder for gradient verification
model_d2_check = build_model(
    depth=2,
    seed=cfg.seeds[0]
).to(device)                                      # Use the same MPS/CPU device selected in Part 0

recorder_check = GradientRecorder(model_d2_check) # Snapshot initial W₁ before any SGD updates

optimizer_check = torch.optim.SGD(
    model_d2_check.parameters(),                  # Optimize only this D2 model's parameters
    lr=cfg.lr,                                    # Provisional learning rate
    momentum=cfg.momentum,                        # 0.0: plain SGD
    weight_decay=cfg.weight_decay                 # 0.0: no weight-decay regularization
)

# Prepare a fixed batch of 8 BloodMNIST images and labels
x_check = sample_images.to(device)                # Images from Section 2.4: [8, 3, 28, 28]

y_check = torch.tensor(
    [torch.as_tensor(train_dataset[i][1]).item() for i in range(8)],
    dtype=torch.long
).to(device)                                      # Ground-truth class labels: [8]

# Calculate gradients for this batch without updating weights yet
model_d2_check.train()                            # Set the model to training mode
optimizer_check.zero_grad()                       # Clear gradients before backward propagation

logits = model_d2_check(x_check)                  # Forward pass: [8, 3, 28, 28] -> [8, 8]
loss = criterion(logits, y_check)                 # Calculate mean CrossEntropyLoss
loss.backward()                                   # Compute gradients for all trainable parameters

# Record gradients BEFORE the SGD update
recorder_check.record(
    model_d2_check,
    epoch=1,
    batch_idx=0
)

# Display the recorded RMS gradient of each hidden layer
for record in recorder_check.step_records:
    print(
        f"Hidden Layer {record['layer']}: "
        f"RMS gradient = {record['grad_rms']:.6e}"
    )

assert len(recorder_check.step_records) == 2      # D2 must produce exactly 2 hidden-layer gradient records

# Check normalized weight change before and after one SGD update
change_before = first_layer_weight_change(
    model_d2_check,
    recorder_check.initial_weight
)                                                 # Must equal 0 before any optimizer step

optimizer_check.step()                            # Update D2 weights and biases using the computed gradients
recorder_check.finish_epoch(model_d2_check, epoch=1)  # Save the first-layer weight change after the update

change_after = recorder_check.weight_change_records[0]["first_layer_weight_change"]

assert change_before == 0.0                       # Initial weights must match their saved snapshot
assert np.isfinite(change_after)                  # Measured weight change must be numerically valid

print(f"\nFirst-layer weight change before update: {change_before:.6e}")
print(f"First-layer weight change after update:  {change_after:.6e}")
print("D2 gradient recorder verification: OK")

4.6 — Verify Gradient Logging Protocol¶

Objective: Verify that the training loop and gradient recorder work together across multiple batches and epochs using the same measurement rules defined in the experimental protocol.

Procedure:

  1. Create a fresh D2 model, SGD optimizer, and GradientRecorder.

  2. Create a separate seeded training DataLoader for this debugging run.

  3. Train D2 for two short debugging epochs, processing 12 batches per epoch.

  4. Record layer-wise RMS gradients during the processed training steps.

  5. Verify that the early-step recorder stores the individual gradient measurements.

  6. Verify that the epoch-level recorder uses only the first 10 batches of each epoch.

  7. Verify that one normalized first-layer weight-change value is recorded at the end of each epoch.

  8. Check that all recorded values are finite.

Expected Result:

For a 2-epoch debugging run with 12 batches per epoch and 2 hidden layers:

  • 24 global training steps.
  • 48 early-step gradient records (24 steps × 2 hidden layers).
  • 4 epoch-level gradient summaries (2 epochs × 2 hidden layers).
  • 10 sampled batches per epoch for each hidden layer's epoch-level gradient summary.
  • 2 normalized first-layer weight-change records.

Purpose: Confirm that the gradient recorder correctly follows the logging protocol before it is used in the main depth and activation experiments.

Fixed Logging Protocol:

  • First 100 global training steps: Record gradients at every step.
  • Every epoch: Calculate mean RMS gradients from the first 10 batches.
  • End of every epoch: Record normalized first-layer weight change.

Important Notes:

  • The debugging run contains only 24 steps, so it verifies the early-step recording behavior but does not yet exercise the 100-step cutoff.
  • The full 100-step recording limit will be exercised and checked in the subsequent full-pipeline tests.
  • The recorder must be initialized before the model's first optimizer update.
  • The same logging rules must remain fixed across D2/D5/D10/D20 and Sigmoid/Tanh/ReLU.
  • Results from this debugging run are not used for the final research conclusions.
In [39]:
# Create a fresh model, optimizer, and recorder for a short logging test
model_d2_logging = build_model(
    depth=2,
    seed=cfg.seeds[0]
).to(device)                                      # New model; do not reuse the partially trained D2

optimizer_logging = torch.optim.SGD(
    model_d2_logging.parameters(),                # Optimizer tied to this model only
    lr=cfg.lr,
    momentum=cfg.momentum,
    weight_decay=cfg.weight_decay
)

recorder_logging = GradientRecorder(
    model_d2_logging,
    first_steps=100,                              # Log each of the first 100 global training steps
    epoch_batches=10                              # Average gradients from first 10 batches per epoch
)

# Create an independent seeded DataLoader for this debugging run
debug_loader = DataLoader(
    train_dataset,                                # Official BloodMNIST training split
    batch_size=cfg.batch_size,                    # Use the same batch size as the main experiments
    shuffle=True,                                 # Shuffle training images

)

# Test gradient logging across two short epochs
debug_epochs = 2
debug_batches = 12

for epoch in range(1, debug_epochs + 1):

    train_loss = train_one_epoch(
        model=model_d2_logging,
        loader=debug_loader,
        criterion=criterion,
        optimizer=optimizer_logging,
        device=device,
        max_batches=debug_batches,                # Process 12 batches in each debugging epoch
        recorder=recorder_logging,                # Activate layer-wise gradient measurements
        epoch=epoch                               # Label measurements with the current epoch
    )

    weight_change = recorder_logging.weight_change_records[-1]["first_layer_weight_change"]

    print(
        f"Epoch {epoch}: "
        f"Train Loss = {train_loss:.4f}, "
        f"First-Layer Weight Change = {weight_change:.6e}"
    )

# Verify the number of saved gradient and weight-change measurements
step_records = recorder_logging.step_records
epoch_records = recorder_logging.epoch_mean_records()
weight_records = recorder_logging.weight_change_records

assert recorder_logging.global_step == 24         # 2 epochs × 12 optimizer steps
assert len(step_records) == 24 * 2                 # 24 steps × 2 hidden layers
assert len(epoch_records) == 2 * 2                 # 2 epochs × 2 hidden layers
assert len(weight_records) == 2                    # One weight-change measurement per epoch

assert all(record["batches"] == 10 for record in epoch_records)  # Exactly 10 samples per layer/epoch

# Verify all recorded metrics are finite
assert all(np.isfinite(record["grad_rms"]) for record in step_records)
assert all(np.isfinite(record["mean_grad_rms"]) for record in epoch_records)
assert all(np.isfinite(record["first_layer_weight_change"]) for record in weight_records)

print("\nEarly-step records:", len(step_records))
print("Epoch-level gradient records:", len(epoch_records))
print("Weight-change records:", len(weight_records))
print("Gradient logging protocol: OK")

Part 5 — Pipeline Verification & Experimental Protocol Finalization¶

1. Overview & Research Objective¶

Part 5 integrates the data pipeline, configurable MLP, training and validation functions, and gradient-measurement system developed in Parts 1–4.

The objective is to verify that these components operate correctly together and finalize a consistent experimental protocol before conducting the main depth and activation comparisons.

This part introduces a reusable experiment runner, performs an end-to-end smoke test, evaluates the suitability of the proposed learning rate, and establishes a predefined training-loss threshold.

The smoke test and pilot runs are used for pipeline verification and protocol selection, not as evidence for the research hypotheses.

2. Workflow & Section Guide¶

Section Main Task Purpose
5.1 — End-to-End Pipeline Smoke Test Define make_train_loader(seed) and run_training(); execute a short D2 test with gradient recording. Verify integrated model training, validation, measurement logging, and result collection.
5.2 — Learning-Rate Sanity Pilot Train D2 and D20 for three complete epochs using the proposed learning rate. Check for obvious numerical or optimization instability across the shallowest and deepest architectures.
5.3 — Freeze Primary Learning Rate Review pilot results and finalize cfg.lr = 0.1. Establish one common learning rate for the main experiments.
5.4 — Select Training-Loss Threshold Define epochs-to-threshold using a predefined loss threshold of 1.50. Establish a consistent measure of training-loss reduction speed.
5.5 — Finalize Experimental Configuration Set cfg.loss_threshold = 1.50 and verify the remaining experimental settings. Document the fixed protocol applied in Stage A and Stage B.

3. Experimental Protocol & Controls¶

3.1 Pipeline Verification¶

Section 5.1 combines the components developed in earlier parts:

  • Part 1: Experimental configuration, BloodMNIST datasets, and DataLoaders.
  • Part 2: Configurable MLP architecture and controlled initialization through build_model().
  • Part 3: SGD training and validation procedures.
  • Part 4: GradientRecorder and early-layer weight-displacement measurements.

The reusable run_training() function coordinates model construction, seeded data loading, optimizer creation, training, validation, measurement recording, and result collection.

Each independent training run uses a freshly initialized model, an associated optimizer, a seeded training DataLoader, and a new gradient recorder.

The initial smoke test uses D2, seed 0, one training pass limited to 12 batches, and validation to verify the integrated pipeline.

3.2 Learning-Rate Sanity Pilot¶

Sections 5.2–5.3 assess the proposed learning rate using the shallowest (D2) and deepest (D20) Sigmoid MLPs.

Both models use:

  • Xavier Uniform initialization.
  • SGD without momentum or weight decay.
  • Learning rate of 0.1.
  • Random seed 0.
  • Three complete training epochs.

The pilot checks for non-finite losses, loss explosion, and obvious optimization instability.

The learning rate is then fixed at 0.1 for all main experimental conditions.

This procedure is a stability check rather than a model-specific learning-rate optimization. Slow learning in a deep network is not, by itself, evidence that the learning rate is unsuitable.

3.3 Training-Loss Threshold¶

Sections 5.4–5.5 establish a predefined training-loss threshold of 1.50 to compare optimization progress across experimental conditions.

For a training run with (E) epochs, define:

$$ T_{\mathrm{threshold}} = \min\left\{ e\in\{1,\ldots,E\}: L_{\mathrm{train}}(e)\leq L^* \right\} $$

where:

  • $L_{\mathrm{train}}(e)$: Sample-weighted mean training loss recorded during epoch (e).
  • $L^*=1.50$: Fixed training-loss threshold.
  • $E=20$: Main-experiment training budget.

If the threshold is not reached within 20 epochs, the result is reported as "Not reached".

Epochs-to-threshold is an operational measure of training-loss reduction speed, not proof of complete convergence or generalization.

The threshold is selected using pilot information and fixed before the main experiments.

3.4 Finalized Main-Experiment Settings¶

Setting Final Protocol
Dataset BloodMNIST official splits
MLP input / hidden width / output 2352 / 256 / 8
Stage A depths D2, D5, D10, D20
Stage A activation Sigmoid
Stage B depth D5
Stage B activations Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU
Weight initialization Xavier Uniform, gain = 1
Optimizer SGD
Learning rate 0.1
Momentum / weight decay 0.0 / 0.0
Training batch size 128
Main training duration 20 complete epochs
Random seeds 0, 1, 2
Early-step gradient recording First 100 global optimizer steps
Epoch-level gradient recording First 10 batches per epoch
First-layer weight displacement Recorded after each epoch
Training-loss threshold 1.50

These settings define the shared experimental protocol. Network depth is varied in Stage A, while activation function is varied at fixed D5 depth in Stage B.

4. Connections to the Main Experiments¶

Part 6 — Stage A: Network Depth

Reuses run_training() and the finalized protocol to compare D2, D5, D10, and D20 across three random seeds.

The recorded gradients, first-layer weight displacement, and training-loss trajectories are used to investigate H1 and H2.

Part 7 — Stage B: Activation Functions

Reuses the same training and measurement procedures to compare Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU at D5, under the common Xavier Uniform initialization.

The D5 Sigmoid baseline from Stage A is reused rather than retrained.

Part 8 — Final Analysis & Reporting

Verifies the completed experimental records and summarizes results across seeds, including gradient attenuation, early-layer trainability, convergence behavior, and validation performance.

5. Outcome & Role in the Experiment¶

Part 5 establishes a verified, reusable experiment runner and a predefined protocol for the controlled comparisons in Parts 6–7.

The primary learning rate and training-loss threshold are fixed before the main experiments, reducing the risk of post hoc methodological adjustments based on the final results.

The pilot and smoke-test observations are kept separate from the main experimental evidence used to evaluate H1, H2, and H3.

5.1 — End-to-End Pipeline Smoke Test¶

Objective: Verify that the complete BloodMNIST training, validation, and gradient-measurement pipeline developed in Parts 0–4 works correctly in a single controlled run before conducting the learning-rate pilot and main experiments.

Procedure:

  1. Define make_train_loader(seed) to create a fresh training DataLoader with an independently seeded random generator. This ensures that each run starts with a reproducible training-data order.

  2. Define a reusable run_training() function that connects the existing components:

    • Create a new model using build_model() from Part 2.
    • Create an independent training DataLoader using the official BloodMNIST training split from Part 1.
    • Initialize a fresh SGD optimizer using the selected learning rate.
    • Initialize a new GradientRecorder from Part 4 before the first optimizer update.
    • Train the model using train_one_epoch() from Part 4.
    • Evaluate the model on the complete official validation split using evaluate() from Part 3.
    • Store training history, validation metrics, layer-wise RMS gradients, and first-layer normalized weight changes.

  3. Perform a short end-to-end smoke test using:

    • Model: D2 (2 hidden Linear layers).
    • Activation: Sigmoid.
    • Initialization: Xavier Uniform.
    • Random seed: 0.
    • Optimizer: SGD with the current provisional learning rate.
    • Training duration: 1 epoch, limited to 12 training batches.
    • Validation: Complete official BloodMNIST validation split.

  4. Verify that the run produces valid outputs:

    • Finite training and validation losses.
    • Finite validation accuracy and macro-F1.
    • Layer-wise RMS gradient records for both hidden layers.
    • Epoch-level gradient summaries using the first 10 training batches.
    • One normalized first-layer weight-change measurement.
    • Correctly structured training history and experiment configuration.

Purpose: Confirm that data loading, model construction, forward propagation, loss calculation, backpropagation, gradient recording, SGD parameter updates, validation, and result storage operate together correctly.

Expected Results:

For 1 debugging epoch containing 12 training batches with a D2 model:

  • 12 optimizer steps.
  • 24 early-step gradient records (12 steps × 2 hidden layers).
  • 2 epoch-level gradient summaries (1 epoch × 2 hidden layers).
  • 10 sampled batches for each hidden layer's epoch-level gradient summary.
  • 1 normalized first-layer weight-change record.
  • 1 training-history entry containing training loss, validation loss, validation accuracy, and validation macro-F1.
  • All recorded numerical measurements are finite.

The exact loss, accuracy, macro-F1, and gradient values are not predetermined. This smoke test checks pipeline correctness rather than model performance.

Role in the Experiment:

Section 5.1 establishes a verified, reusable experiment runner for subsequent stages:

  • Section 5.2: Perform the learning-rate sanity pilot using D2 and D20.
  • Sections 5.3–5.5: Finalize the common learning rate and training-loss threshold.
  • Part 6 — Stage A: Compare D2, D5, D10, and D20 under controlled conditions.
  • Part 7 — Stage B: Compare Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU at a fixed network depth.
  • Part 8: Repeat the main experiments with three random seeds and aggregate the results.

The same training and gradient-logging functions will be reused without changing the experimental protocol.

Important Notes:

  • This is a debugging run, not a learning-rate pilot or main experiment.
  • The learning rate remains provisional; it will be evaluated in Section 5.2.
  • A fresh model, optimizer, DataLoader, and gradient recorder must be created for each independent run.
  • Gradient logging follows the fixed protocol from Part 4: every step during the first 100 global training steps and the first 10 batches of every epoch.
  • Only the official training split is used to update model parameters. The validation split is used only for evaluation.
  • The test split remains untouched.
  • max_batches=12 is used only to limit this smoke test. Main experimental runs will use all training batches by setting max_batches=None.
  • Smoke-test results must not be included in the final experimental comparisons.
In [40]:
# Create a fresh training DataLoader with reproducible batch shuffling
def make_train_loader(seed):

    # Give each run its own random generator for training-data shuffling
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)  # Same seed produces the same initial training-data order

    return DataLoader(
        train_dataset,                               # Official BloodMNIST training split from Part 1
        batch_size=cfg.batch_size,                   # Fixed number of images per training batch
        shuffle=True,                               # Randomly reshuffle training samples each epoch
        generator=generator                          # Use this run's independent random generator
    )


# Run one complete training experiment using the existing Parts 2–4 functions
def run_training(depth, seed, activation=None, lr=None,
                 epochs=None, max_batches=None):

    # Use the project configuration unless a different setting is explicitly provided
    activation = cfg.activation if activation is None else activation  # Default: Sigmoid; Stage B can change it
    lr = cfg.lr if lr is None else lr                  # Default: project LR; Part 5 pilot can test a candidate
    epochs = cfg.epochs if epochs is None else epochs  # Default: 20 full training epochs

    if epochs < 1 or lr <= 0 or (max_batches is not None and max_batches < 1):
        raise ValueError("epochs and lr must be positive; max_batches must be None or positive")

    # Start a fresh, independently reproducible training run
    set_seed(seed)                                      # Set Python, NumPy, and PyTorch random seeds
    loader = make_train_loader(seed)                    # Fresh DataLoader; never reuse an already advanced generator
    model = build_model(
        depth=depth,                                    # Number of hidden Linear layers: D2, D5, D10, or D20
        seed=seed,                                      # Control random model initialization
        activation=activation                           # Use the selected hidden-layer activation
    ).to(device)                                        # Move model parameters to the configured CPU/MPS device

    # Initialize a fresh SGD optimizer for this model
    optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(
        model.parameters(),                             # Weights and biases belonging to this model only
        lr=lr,                                          # Learning rate controlling SGD update size
        momentum=cfg.momentum,                          # 0.0 in the current experimental protocol
        weight_decay=cfg.weight_decay                   # 0.0 in the current experimental protocol
    )

    # Create the recorder BEFORE training so it saves the initial first-layer weights
    recorder = GradientRecorder(
        model,                                          # Measure gradients and weight changes for this model
        first_steps=100,                                # Record every global step during the first 100 steps
        epoch_batches=10                                # Average RMS gradients from each epoch's first 10 batches
    )

    # Train and validate the model; save one history entry after each epoch
    history = []                                        # List of dictionaries containing epoch-level metrics

    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):                  # Epoch numbering starts at 1, not 0

        train_loss = train_one_epoch(
            model=model,                                # Current MLP being trained
            loader=loader,                              # Reproducibly shuffled training batches
            criterion=criterion,                        # CrossEntropyLoss defined in Part 3
            optimizer=optimizer,                        # SGD optimizer for this run
            device=device,                              # Device used by model and image tensors
            max_batches=max_batches,                    # None = full epoch; integer = debugging batch limit
            recorder=recorder,                          # Record hidden-layer gradients and weight changes
            epoch=epoch                                 # Identify the epoch in gradient and weight-change records
        )

        # Evaluate the updated model on the complete validation dataset
        val_metrics = evaluate(
            model=model,                                # Evaluate the model after this epoch's SGD updates
            loader=val_loader,                          # Official validation split; shuffle=False
            criterion=criterion,                        # Same CrossEntropyLoss used during training
            device=device,
            num_classes=cfg.num_classes                 # Eight BloodMNIST classes
        )

        # Save the training and validation metrics for this epoch
        history.append({
            "epoch": epoch,                              # Current training epoch
            "train_loss": train_loss,                    # Mean training loss over processed training images
            "val_loss": val_metrics["loss"],             # Mean loss over the complete validation dataset
            "val_accuracy": val_metrics["accuracy"],     # Correct predictions / total validation images
            "val_macro_f1": val_metrics["macro_f1"]      # Mean of the eight class-specific F1 scores
        })

    # Return the settings and measurements without retraining or recalculating gradients
    return {
        "run_config": {
            "depth": depth,                              # Architecture depth used in this run
            "seed": seed,                                # Random seed used for model and training shuffle
            "activation": activation,                    # Hidden-layer activation function
            "initialization": "xavier_uniform",          # Fixed initialization implemented in Part 2
            "learning_rate": lr,                         # Actual SGD learning rate used
            "epochs": epochs,                            # Number of completed training epochs
            "max_batches": max_batches,                  # Debugging limit; None for full training
            "batch_size": cfg.batch_size,                # Training mini-batch size
            "momentum": cfg.momentum,                    # SGD momentum setting
            "weight_decay": cfg.weight_decay             # SGD weight-decay setting
        },
        "history": history,                              # Training/validation metrics after every epoch
        "step_records": recorder.step_records,           # Hidden-layer RMS gradients from first 100 global steps
        "epoch_gradients": recorder.epoch_mean_records(), # Mean hidden-layer RMS gradients from first 10 batches/epoch
        "weight_changes": recorder.weight_change_records # Normalized Hidden Layer 1 weight change after each epoch
    }


# Run a short D2 smoke test (debugging only, not a main experiment)
smoke_run = run_training(
    depth=2,                                            # Use the shallowest baseline model, D2
    seed=cfg.seeds[0],                                  # Use the first configured seed (0)
    epochs=1,                                           # One debugging epoch
    max_batches=12                                      # Train on only 12 batches, not the full dataset
)

# Read the results stored by the reusable experiment runner
smoke_history = smoke_run["history"][0]                  # First and only epoch's training/validation metrics
step_records = smoke_run["step_records"]                 # Early-step gradient records for both hidden layers
epoch_records = smoke_run["epoch_gradients"]             # Epoch-level mean RMS gradient records
weight_records = smoke_run["weight_changes"]             # First-hidden-layer normalized weight change

# Verify that the smoke test produced the expected number of records
assert len(smoke_run["history"]) == 1                    # Exactly one training-history entry
assert len(step_records) == 12 * 2                       # 12 steps × 2 hidden layers = 24 records
assert len(epoch_records) == 1 * 2                       # 1 epoch × 2 hidden layers = 2 summaries
assert all(r["batches"] == 10 for r in epoch_records)    # Each epoch summary uses exactly 10 batches
assert len(weight_records) == 1                          # One normalized weight-change value after the epoch

# Verify that all losses, classification metrics, and gradient measurements are finite
assert all(np.isfinite(smoke_history[k]) for k in
           ["train_loss", "val_loss", "val_accuracy", "val_macro_f1"])

assert all(np.isfinite(r["grad_rms"]) for r in step_records)  # No NaN/Inf in per-step RMS gradients
assert all(np.isfinite(r["mean_grad_rms"]) for r in epoch_records)  # No NaN/Inf in epoch gradient summaries
assert all(np.isfinite(r["first_layer_weight_change"]) for r in weight_records)  # Valid normalized weight change

# Display a compact summary of the completed end-to-end smoke test
print("=== Section 5.1 — End-to-End Pipeline Smoke Test ===")
print(f"Model: D2 | Seed: {cfg.seeds[0]} | Epochs: 1 | Training Batches: 12")
print(f"Train Loss:   {smoke_history['train_loss']:.4f}")
print(f"Val Loss:     {smoke_history['val_loss']:.4f}")
print(f"Val Accuracy: {smoke_history['val_accuracy']:.4f}")
print(f"Val Macro-F1: {smoke_history['val_macro_f1']:.4f}")
print(f"Early-Step Gradient Records: {len(step_records)}")
print(f"Epoch-Level Gradient Records: {len(epoch_records)}")
print(f"Weight-Change Records:       {len(weight_records)}")
print(f"First-Layer Weight Change:   {weight_records[0]['first_layer_weight_change']:.6e}")
print("\nEnd-to-end pipeline smoke test: OK")

5.2 — Learning-Rate Sanity Pilot¶

Objective: Verify that the provisional learning rate provides numerically stable training for both the shallowest and deepest MLP architectures before selecting one common learning rate for the main experiments.

Procedure:

  1. Select the two extreme network depths from the experimental configuration:

    • D2: 2 hidden Linear layers (shallowest network).
    • D20: 20 hidden Linear layers (deepest network).

  2. Use the same controlled training settings for both models:

    • Dataset: BloodMNIST official training and validation splits.
    • Hidden width: 256 neurons per hidden layer.
    • Activation: Sigmoid.
    • Initialization: Xavier Uniform (gain = 1), with zero biases.
    • Loss function: CrossEntropyLoss.
    • Optimizer: SGD, with the configured momentum and weight decay.
    • Learning rate: the current provisional value (cfg.lr = 0.1).
    • Random seed: 0.
    • Training duration: 3 complete epochs.
    • Batch size: 128.
    • Gradient logging: the fixed protocol implemented in Part 4.

  3. Use the reusable run_training() function from Section 5.1 to train D2 and D20 independently. Each run must start with a freshly initialized model, optimizer, training DataLoader, and gradient recorder.

  4. Record the training loss and validation loss after each epoch. Retain the complete results returned by run_training() for later reference.

  5. Examine both models for signs of optimization instability:

    • Does training loss become NaN or infinity?
    • Do RMS gradient measurements become non-finite?
    • Does training loss increase dramatically or fluctuate excessively?
    • Is there evidence of numerical divergence or unstable optimization?

  6. If the initial learning rate produces clear instability, test only 2–3 reasonable learning-rate candidates using the same procedure. Otherwise, do not perform additional learning-rate trials.

  7. Do not select a separate learning rate for each depth. Do not interpret poor convergence in D20 alone as proof that the learning rate is unsuitable.

Purpose: Reduce the risk that the observed differences between shallow and deep networks are caused primarily by an obviously unstable learning rate rather than by depth-dependent gradient propagation.

Expected Results:

  • Two independent pilot runs: D2 and D20.
  • Three training-loss measurements per model, one for each completed epoch.
  • Three validation-loss measurements per model.
  • Finite training losses, validation losses, and recorded RMS gradients for numerically stable runs.
  • A small results table showing how training and validation losses change across epochs for each depth.
  • Identification of any learning-rate candidate that causes clear numerical or optimization instability.

D2 may improve faster than D20. D20 may exhibit very slow learning or nearly constant training loss because of gradient vanishing. Such behavior is an important observation, but it does not automatically indicate an unsuitable learning rate.

Role in the Experiment:

This section provides evidence for selecting one common learning rate in Section 5.3 — Freeze Primary Learning Rate.

The selected learning rate will subsequently be held constant across:

  • Part 6 — Stage A: D2, D5, D10, and D20 (depth comparison).
  • Part 7 — Stage B: Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU at a fixed depth (activation comparison).
  • Part 8: Three-seed repetitions of the main experimental conditions.

The pilot's training-loss trajectories may also inform the predefined convergence threshold selected in Section 5.4.

Important Notes:

  • This is a learning-rate sanity pilot, not the main depth experiment.
  • Use complete training epochs (max_batches=None), rather than the limited 12 batches used in Section 5.1.
  • The learning rate remains provisional until Section 5.3.
  • Do not change cfg.lr or cfg.loss_threshold in this section.
  • Do not reuse trained pilot models in Stage A or Stage B.
  • Do not use the official test split.
  • Do not include pilot metrics in the final three-seed experimental averages.
  • Do not add extensive learning-rate sweeps, alternative optimizers, or additional network architectures.
In [41]:
# Set up a small learning-rate pilot; keep the project configuration unchanged
pilot_seed = cfg.seeds[0]                               # Use seed 0 for both depths to control randomness
pilot_depths = (min(cfg.depths), max(cfg.depths))        # D2 and D20: shallowest and deepest MLPs
pilot_epochs = 3                                        # Run three COMPLETE training epochs per model
pilot_learning_rates = (cfg.lr,)                        # Start with the provisional LR (0.1); no automatic LR sweep

# Prepare containers for completed runs, epoch losses, and numerical failures
lr_pilot_runs = {}                                      # Key: (learning_rate, depth); value: full run_training() result
lr_pilot_rows = []                                      # One row per completed epoch, for a readable loss table
lr_pilot_failures = []                                  # Save only clearly identified numerical failures

# Train both depth extremes independently under the SAME candidate learning rate
for learning_rate in pilot_learning_rates:              # Normally one LR; add alternatives only if instability is observed
    for depth in pilot_depths:                          # Compare D2 and D20, not the intermediate depths
        print(f"\nPilot: D{depth} | LR={learning_rate:g} | Seed={pilot_seed} | Epochs={pilot_epochs}")

        try:
            pilot_run = run_training(
                depth=depth,                            # Change only network depth between the two models
                seed=pilot_seed,                        # Same random seed for both independent runs
                activation="sigmoid",                   # Stage A baseline activation, fixed during the pilot
                lr=learning_rate,                       # Test the same candidate LR for D2 and D20
                epochs=pilot_epochs,                    # Train for three complete epochs
                max_batches=None                        # None means ALL training batches, not a smoke-test subset
            )
        except ValueError as error:
            error_message = str(error)                  # Read the numerical error raised in Parts 3–4
            if ("Training loss is NaN or infinite" not in error_message
                    and "Non-finite gradient RMS" not in error_message):
                raise                                  # Do not hide unrelated bugs as LR instability
            lr_pilot_failures.append({"lr": learning_rate, "depth": depth, "reason": error_message})
            print(f"Numerical failure in D{depth}: {error_message}")
            continue                                   # Keep the failure documented; inspect before changing LR

        # Preserve the full measurements and collect the loss trajectory for inspection
        lr_pilot_runs[(learning_rate, depth)] = pilot_run  # Keep history and gradient measurements for later review
        for metrics in pilot_run["history"]:              # One dictionary of train/validation metrics per epoch
            lr_pilot_rows.append({
                "lr": learning_rate,                    # Learning rate tested in this run
                "depth": f"D{depth}",                   # Label D2 or D20 for easier comparison
                "epoch": metrics["epoch"],              # Epoch number: 1, 2, or 3
                "train_loss": metrics["train_loss"],    # Mean training CrossEntropyLoss for the full epoch
                "val_loss": metrics["val_loss"]         # Mean CrossEntropyLoss on the full validation split
            })

# Display one compact table; do not automatically select or freeze the learning rate
lr_pilot_df = pd.DataFrame(lr_pilot_rows)               # Convert epoch dictionaries into a pandas table
print("\n=== Section 5.2 — Learning-Rate Sanity Pilot ===")
if not lr_pilot_df.empty:                               # A run may fail before completing its first epoch
    print(lr_pilot_df.round(4).to_string(index=False))  # Show epoch-by-epoch losses for D2 and D20
    losses = lr_pilot_df[["train_loss", "val_loss"]].to_numpy()  # Extract numerical losses for a finite-value check
    if np.isfinite(losses).all():                        # True only when every displayed loss is finite
        print("\nAll completed epoch-level losses are finite.")
    else:
        print("\nWARNING: Non-finite epoch-level loss detected. Investigate before freezing LR.")

# Report failures explicitly; finite losses alone do not prove that optimization is stable
for failure in lr_pilot_failures:
    print(f"WARNING: D{failure['depth']} at LR={failure['lr']:g}: {failure['reason']}")
print("Review the loss trajectories for explosion or strong oscillation before Section 5.3.")
print("Learning rate is NOT frozen; cfg.lr is unchanged.")

5.2.1 — Pilot Loss Results & Interpretation¶

Pilot Configuration:

  • Learning rate: 0.1 (provisional).
  • Models: D2 and D20.
  • Activation: Sigmoid.
  • Initialization: Xavier Uniform.
  • Optimizer: SGD.
  • Random seed: 0.
  • Training duration: 3 complete epochs per model.

Observed Results:

Model Train Loss (Epoch 1) Train Loss (Epoch 3) Val Loss (Epoch 1) Val Loss (Epoch 3)
D2 1.5425 0.9607 1.2679 0.8822
D20 2.0331 2.0258 2.1165 2.0188

Interpretation:

  • D2: Training loss decreased from 1.5425 to 0.9607, while validation loss decreased from 1.2679 to 0.8822. This indicates that the shallow network learned successfully without obvious learning-rate instability during the pilot.
  • D20: Training loss decreased only slightly from 2.0331 to 2.0258. This indicates very slow learning or optimization difficulty in the deep network.
  • All recorded epoch-level training and validation losses were finite. No loss explosion or numerical divergence was observed in the completed pilot runs.

Preliminary Conclusion:

The provisional learning rate of 0.1 did not produce obvious numerical instability in either network over three epochs. However, D20 showed substantially slower learning than D2.

Slow convergence in D20 does not necessarily indicate an unsuitable learning rate. Because the deep Sigmoid network may experience vanishing gradients, additional inspection of the gradient measurements already collected during the pilot can help interpret this behavior.

Additional Gradient Inspection:

To investigate whether the nearly constant training loss in D20 is associated with gradient attenuation, the next cell retrieves the recorded RMS gradients from Hidden Layer 1 (closest to the input) and Hidden Layer 20 (closest to the output).

This inspection:

  • Uses existing gradient records from the completed D20 pilot.
  • Does not train another model or perform an additional experiment.
  • Does not change the learning rate or any experimental settings.
  • Provides preliminary evidence for interpretation, not final hypothesis testing.

The main depth-dependent gradient analysis will be conducted in Stage A.
