5.2.2 — D20 Gradient Findings & Learning-Rate Pilot Conclusion¶

Observed Gradient Measurements:

The following values represent the mean RMS weight gradients recorded from the first 10 training batches of each epoch, as defined by the gradient-logging protocol in Part 4.

Epoch Hidden Layer 1 RMS Hidden Layer 20 RMS
1 3.066 × 10⁻¹⁵ 1.068 × 10⁻³
2 3.092 × 10⁻¹⁵ 1.392 × 10⁻³
3 3.005 × 10⁻¹⁵ 1.195 × 10⁻³

Interpretation:

  • Hidden Layer 1 exhibited extremely small RMS weight gradients, approximately (3 \times 10^{-15}), throughout the pilot.
  • Hidden Layer 20 exhibited much larger RMS gradients, approximately (10^{-3}).
  • The RMS gradient magnitude at Hidden Layer 20 was approximately 348–450 billion times larger than at Hidden Layer 1.
  • This substantial difference provides preliminary evidence of severe early-layer gradient attenuation in the D20 Sigmoid network.
  • The observed attenuation is consistent with D20's nearly constant training loss and suggests difficulty updating its early-layer weights.

However, gradient attenuation alone does not establish the complete cause of poor convergence. The main experiments will examine layer-wise RMS gradients, normalized early-layer weight changes, training-loss trajectories, and validation performance together.

Learning-Rate Sanity Pilot Conclusion:

The provisional learning rate of 0.1 produced finite training and validation losses in both D2 and D20 during three complete training epochs.

D2 showed clear learning progress, while D20 showed slow convergence and extremely small early-layer gradients. No obvious numerical instability attributable to an excessively large learning rate was observed.

Based on the limited sanity pilot, there is no clear justification for testing additional learning rates. The observed D20 behavior is consistent with the gradient-vanishing phenomenon being investigated, rather than demonstrating learning-rate instability.

Recommendation for Section 5.3:

Retain learning rate = 0.1 as the proposed common primary learning rate for Stage A and Stage B.

The learning rate has not yet been formally frozen. Section 5.3 will document the selection and finalize the configuration before the main experiments.

Limitations of the Pilot:

  • Only one random seed and three training epochs were used.
  • The pilot is a stability check, not a comprehensive learning-rate search.
  • The gradient findings are preliminary and must not be treated as the final evidence for hypotheses H1 and H2.

5.3 — Freeze Primary Learning Rate¶

Objective: Select and freeze one primary learning rate based on the learning-rate sanity pilot in Section 5.2, ensuring that all main experimental conditions use the same learning rate.

Procedure:

  1. Review the learning-rate sanity pilot results from Section 5.2:

    • Candidate learning rate: 0.1.
    • Models tested: D2 and D20.
    • Activation: Sigmoid.
    • Initialization: Xavier Uniform.
    • Optimizer: SGD.
    • Random seed: 0.
    • Training duration: 3 complete epochs per model.

  2. Confirm that both pilot runs completed successfully and produced finite training and validation losses.

  3. Review the observed training behavior:

    • D2: Training loss decreased from 1.5425 to 0.9607, indicating clear learning progress without obvious numerical instability.
    • D20: Training loss decreased slightly from 2.0331 to 2.0258, indicating slow learning without loss explosion.
    • Gradient inspection: D20 exhibited extremely small early-layer RMS gradients (approximately (3 \times 10^{-15})), consistent with severe gradient attenuation.

  4. Select learning rate = 0.1 as the common primary learning rate. No additional learning-rate candidates are required because the initial candidate did not show obvious numerical instability.

  5. Verify that the selected learning rate was successfully tested on both D2 and D20, then store the selected value in cfg.lr.

  6. Keep the selected learning rate fixed across all main experimental conditions:

    • Stage A: D2, D5, D10, and D20.
    • Stage B: Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU at the selected fixed depth.
    • Multi-seed analysis: Repeat the main conditions using the same primary learning rate across all three random seeds.

Purpose: Prevent learning-rate differences from confounding the depth and activation comparisons. A common learning rate allows the study to investigate gradient propagation, early-layer trainability, and convergence under controlled optimization settings.

Expected Results:

  • Both D2 and D20 pilot runs are verified.
  • The selected primary learning rate is confirmed as 0.1.
  • cfg.lr is set to 0.1.
  • The existing SGD optimizer configuration remains unchanged:
    • Learning rate: 0.1.
    • Momentum: 0.0.
    • Weight decay: 0.0.
  • No additional model training is performed.
  • The learning rate is documented as fixed for the main experiments.

Role in the Experiment:

Section 5.3 finalizes the primary learning rate before the main depth and activation experiments.

  • Section 5.4: Use the completed pilot observations to select a predefined training-loss threshold for the convergence metric.
  • Section 5.5: Freeze the loss threshold and finalize the remaining experimental configuration.
  • Part 6 — Stage A: Compare network depths while keeping the learning rate fixed at 0.1.
  • Part 7 — Stage B: Compare activation functions using the same learning rate.
  • Part 8: Repeat the main experimental conditions across three random seeds without changing the learning-rate protocol.

Important Notes:

  • The selected learning rate is fixed by the experimental protocol, not by making the Python configuration object immutable.
  • The pilot establishes that 0.1 is a reasonable primary learning rate under the tested conditions; it does not establish that 0.1 is globally optimal.
  • Slow convergence in D20 is not, by itself, evidence that the learning rate is unsuitable.
  • Do not tune learning rates separately for individual depths, activation functions, or random seeds.
  • All main experimental runs must start with fresh models and optimizers.
  • The training-loss threshold remains unselected until Section 5.4.

5.4 — Select Training-Loss Threshold¶

Objective: Select a predefined training-loss threshold from the completed learning-rate pilot to measure and compare convergence speed consistently across all main experimental conditions.

Procedure:

  1. Review the training-loss trajectories from the completed D2 and D20 pilot runs in Section 5.2, using the primary learning rate finalized in Section 5.3.

  2. Use the same controlled pilot configuration:

    • Models: D2 and D20.
    • Activation: Sigmoid.
    • Initialization: Xavier Uniform.
    • Optimizer: SGD.
    • Learning rate: 0.1 (fixed in Section 5.3).
    • Random seed: 0.
    • Training duration: 3 complete epochs per model.

  3. Inspect the pilot training-loss values:

    • D2: 1.5425 → 1.1453 → 0.9607.
    • D20: 2.0331 → 2.0299 → 2.0258.

  4. Propose a training-loss threshold of 1.50, based on the pilot observations:

    • It represents a meaningful reduction below the cross-entropy of uniform predictions over eight classes, (\ln(8) \approx 2.079).
    • It lies within the decreasing training-loss trajectory observed for D2.
    • D2 reached this level during the pilot, while D20 did not.
    • The threshold is selected before observing the main experimental results.

  5. Define the convergence metric, epochs-to-threshold, as the first epoch whose mean training loss is less than or equal to the predefined threshold:

    $$ T_{\mathrm{threshold}} = \min\left\{ t \in \{1,\ldots,E\}: L_{\mathrm{train}}(t)\leq L^* \right\} $$

    where:

    • $t$: Training epoch index, starting from 1.
    • $E$: Total number of training epochs (20 for the main experiments).
    • $L_{\mathrm{train}}(t)$: Sample-weighted mean training loss recorded during epoch (t).
    • $L^*$: Predefined training-loss threshold (proposed value: 1.50).
    • $T_{\mathrm{threshold}}$: First epoch at which the training loss reaches or falls below the threshold.

  6. Check when D2 and D20 first reached the proposed threshold during their three-epoch pilot runs.

  7. Keep the proposed threshold separate from cfg.loss_threshold until Section 5.5, where the threshold will be formally frozen.

Purpose: Establish an objective, consistently applied convergence measurement that helps evaluate whether stronger early-layer gradient attenuation is associated with slower learning.

Expected Results:

  • Proposed training-loss threshold: 1.50.
  • D2 first reaches the threshold at epoch 2 in the pilot.
  • D20 does not reach the threshold during the three-epoch pilot.
  • A compact summary of the pilot losses and threshold-reaching epochs.
  • No additional training, validation, or gradient measurements.
  • cfg.loss_threshold remains unchanged until Section 5.5.

Role in the Experiment:

This section defines the convergence metric used to evaluate H2 — Early-Layer Trainability Effect, alongside layer-wise RMS gradients and normalized first-layer weight changes.

The predefined threshold will be used consistently in:

  • Section 5.5: Freeze the selected training-loss threshold and finalize the experimental configuration.
  • Part 6 — Stage A: Compare epochs-to-threshold across D2, D5, D10, and D20.
  • Part 7 — Stage B: Compare convergence across Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU at a fixed depth.
  • Part 8: Aggregate convergence results across three random seeds, while clearly reporting runs that do not reach the threshold.

Important Notes:

  • Use training loss, not validation loss or test loss, to calculate epochs-to-threshold.
  • Use the sample-weighted mean training loss returned by train_one_epoch() in Part 4, not the loss from an individual mini-batch.
  • The recorded training loss is averaged over batches processed during the epoch, while model parameters are being updated.
  • A model reaches the threshold when its recorded epoch-level training loss is less than or equal to 1.50.
  • If a model does not reach the threshold within the fixed training budget, report "Not reached" rather than assigning it an artificial convergence epoch.
  • The threshold is an operational convergence milestone, not a guarantee of high classification accuracy or successful generalization.
  • No threshold tuning is permitted after examining the main experimental results.
  • The official test split remains untouched.
  • This section only analyzes existing pilot measurements and does not introduce an additional experiment.
In [45]:
# Select a training-loss threshold from the completed pilot, before the main experiments
proposed_loss_threshold = 1.50                       # Proposed convergence milestone, measured using mean training CrossEntropyLoss

assert np.isfinite(proposed_loss_threshold) and proposed_loss_threshold > 0  # Require a finite, positive threshold

# Read the existing D2/D20 pilot histories without training additional models
threshold_pilot_rows = []                           # Store one summary dictionary for each pilot model

for depth in pilot_depths:                          # Check D2 and D20, the two depth extremes tested in Section 5.2
    pilot_history = lr_pilot_runs[(cfg.lr, depth)]["history"]  # Retrieve epoch-level metrics for this depth at the frozen LR

    assert len(pilot_history) == pilot_epochs        # Verify that all three pilot epochs were completed
    assert all(
        np.isfinite(row["train_loss"]) for row in pilot_history  # Every epoch must have a finite mean training loss
    )

    # Find the FIRST epoch where the model reaches the proposed loss threshold
    first_reached_epoch = None                      # None means the threshold has not been reached

    for row in pilot_history:                       # Examine recorded epochs in chronological order
        if row["train_loss"] <= proposed_loss_threshold:  # Check whether mean training loss is at or below 1.50
            first_reached_epoch = row["epoch"]       # Save the first epoch satisfying the convergence condition
            break                                   # Stop searching; later epochs cannot be the first to reach it

    # Save a compact summary of each model's pilot loss and threshold-reaching epoch
    threshold_pilot_rows.append({
        "model": f"D{depth}",                        # Model name, such as "D2" or "D20"
        "epoch_1_loss": pilot_history[0]["train_loss"],   # Mean training loss after the first recorded epoch
        "last_epoch_loss": pilot_history[-1]["train_loss"], # Mean training loss during the final pilot epoch
        "first_epoch_at_threshold": (
            first_reached_epoch if first_reached_epoch is not None else "Not reached"
        )                                           # Preserve the actual epoch, or report "Not reached"
    })

# Display the threshold-selection summary without changing the shared configuration
threshold_pilot_df = pd.DataFrame(threshold_pilot_rows)  # Convert the summary dictionaries into a readable table

print("=== Section 5.4 — Select Training-Loss Threshold ===")
print(f"Proposed threshold (training loss): {proposed_loss_threshold:.2f}")
print(threshold_pilot_df.to_string(
    index=False,                                    # Hide the automatically generated pandas row index
    float_format=lambda x: f"{x:.4f}"               # Show loss values with four decimal places
))

print(f"cfg.loss_threshold (not yet frozen): {cfg.loss_threshold}")  # Expected: None until Section 5.5
print("No additional training was performed.")

5.5 — Freeze Loss Threshold & Finalize Configuration¶

Objective: Freeze the training-loss threshold selected in Section 5.4 and verify that the experimental configuration is finalized before conducting the main depth and activation experiments.

Procedure:

  1. Review the experimental decisions established in Sections 5.2–5.4:

    • Primary learning rate: 0.1, finalized in Section 5.3.
    • Proposed training-loss threshold: 1.50, selected from the pilot results in Section 5.4.
    • D2 reached the proposed threshold at epoch 2 during the three-epoch pilot.
    • D20 did not reach the proposed threshold during the three-epoch pilot.

  2. Verify that the learning rate and proposed threshold are valid and consistent with the pilot-based decisions.

  3. Freeze the training-loss threshold by assigning the selected value to cfg.loss_threshold:

    cfg.loss_threshold = proposed_loss_threshold

  4. Verify the main experimental settings:

    • Dataset: BloodMNIST using the official training, validation, and test splits.
    • Network depths: D2, D5, D10, and D20.
    • Hidden width: 256 neurons per hidden layer.
    • Number of output classes: 8.
    • Stage A activation: Sigmoid.
    • Weight initialization: Xavier Uniform (gain = 1), with zero biases.
    • Optimizer: SGD.
    • Learning rate: 0.1.
    • Momentum: 0.0.
    • Weight decay: 0.0.
    • Batch size: 128.
    • Training duration: 20 complete epochs per main run.
    • Random seeds: 0, 1, and 2.
    • Gradient logging: every step during the first 100 global training steps.
    • Epoch-level gradient logging: mean RMS gradients over the first 10 training batches of each epoch.

  5. Print the finalized configuration to document the experimental protocol before the main experiments.

  6. Keep the learning rate, training-loss threshold, gradient-logging rules, and other controlled settings unchanged throughout the main experimental comparisons.

Purpose: Prevent changes in experimental settings after observing the main results, ensuring that differences in gradient propagation, early-layer trainability, and convergence can be interpreted under a consistent experimental protocol.

Expected Results:

  • Primary learning rate confirmed as 0.1.
  • Training-loss threshold frozen at 1.50.
  • cfg.loss_threshold updated from None to 1.50.
  • All required main experimental settings successfully verified.
  • A printed summary of the finalized experimental configuration.
  • No additional model training or hyperparameter tuning.

The predefined convergence metric is:

$$ T_{\mathrm{threshold}} = \min\left\{ t \in \{1,\ldots,E\}: L_{\mathrm{train}}(t)\leq 1.50 \right\} $$

where:

  • $t$: Training epoch index, starting from 1.
  • $E=20$: Fixed number of main training epochs.
  • $L_{\mathrm{train}}(t)$: Sample-weighted mean training loss recorded during epoch $t$.
  • $T_{\mathrm{threshold}}$: First epoch at which the recorded training loss reaches or falls below 1.50.

If the threshold is not reached within 20 epochs, the result is recorded as "Not reached", not as epoch 20.

Role in the Experiment:

Section 5.5 completes Part 5 — Pipeline Smoke Test & Pilot Configuration and establishes the finalized experimental protocol for subsequent analyses.

  • Part 6 — Stage A: Compare D2, D5, D10, and D20 while keeping all other experimental settings fixed. The main independent variable is network depth.
  • Part 7 — Stage B: Compare Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU under the same initialization and optimization settings, using a fixed depth selected from Stage A.
  • Part 8 — Multi-Seed Analysis & Final Report: Repeat the main experimental conditions across three random seeds, aggregate the relevant measurements, and report the results.

The frozen threshold supports H2 — Early-Layer Trainability Effect by allowing convergence speed to be compared alongside layer-wise RMS gradients and normalized first-layer weight changes.

Important Notes:

  • Freezing the threshold is an experimental decision; it does not make the Python configuration object immutable.
  • Do not adjust the threshold separately for different network depths, activation functions, or random seeds.
  • Do not change the threshold after examining Stage A or Stage B results.
  • The threshold is an operational training-loss milestone, not a classification accuracy target.
  • Use the same training-loss measurement implemented in Part 4 for every experimental run.
  • The model, optimizer, and gradient recorder must be initialized independently for each run.
  • The Stage B depth will be selected after Stage A; it is not fixed in this section.
  • The official test split must not be used for training, pilot decisions, or hyperparameter selection.
  • Section 5.5 does not train any additional models. It only finalizes and documents the configuration.

Part 6 — Stage A: Network Depth Experiment¶

1. Overview & Research Objective¶

Stage A investigates how increasing MLP depth affects layer-wise weight-gradient magnitudes, early-layer trainability, and optimization behavior on BloodMNIST.

Four constant-width MLPs with 2, 5, 10, and 20 hidden layers are compared under a shared Sigmoid–Xavier–SGD configuration.

The experiment addresses two hypotheses:

  • H1 — Depth Effect: Increasing network depth is expected to produce stronger attenuation of early-layer weight gradients relative to later hidden layers.
  • H2 — Trainability Effect: Conditions exhibiting stronger early-layer gradient attenuation are expected to show smaller first-layer weight displacement and slower training-loss reduction.

Layer-wise gradient measurements, parameter displacement, training-loss trajectories, and validation metrics are examined together to evaluate these hypotheses.

2. Experimental Design & Controls¶

Independent variable: Number of hidden layers — D2, D5, D10, or D20.

All other main experimental settings follow the protocol finalized in Part 5.

Component Experimental Setting
Dataset BloodMNIST, official training and validation splits
Preprocessing Shared normalization using training-derived RGB statistics
MLP architecture Input: 2352; hidden width: 256; output: 8 classes
Hidden activation Sigmoid
Weight initialization Xavier Uniform, gain = 1
Bias initialization Zeros
Loss function CrossEntropyLoss
Optimizer SGD
Learning rate 0.1
Momentum / weight decay 0.0 / 0.0
Training batch size 128
Training duration 20 complete epochs
Random seeds 0, 1, 2
Gradient recording First 100 global steps; first 10 batches per epoch
Training-loss threshold 1.50

Each depth is trained with three random seeds, producing 12 depth–seed runs.

Every run uses a freshly initialized model, its own optimizer, a seeded training DataLoader, and a gradient recorder. The official test split remains unused in the Stage A analysis.

Hidden width and the training protocol are held fixed; however, model parameter counts necessarily increase with depth. The findings therefore characterize depth-dependent behavior within this MLP architecture family.

3. Workflow & Section Guide¶

Section Main Task Research Purpose

6.2 — Complete Multi-Seed Runs Reuse seed-0 results and complete seeds 1 and 2. Obtain 12 controlled depth–seed runs.
6.3 — Organize Experimental Results Construct analysis DataFrames and aggregate metrics across seeds. Prepare consistent measurements for analysis and visualization.
6.4 — Figure 1: Gradient Magnitude vs. Layer Compare absolute and relative RMS weight gradients across depths. Evaluate H1 using epoch-1 layer-wise measurements.
6.5 — Figure 2: Gradient Evolution Visualize D20 layer-wise gradients across 20 epochs. Examine the persistence of gradient attenuation during training.
6.6 — Figure 3: Training Loss Curves Compare training-loss trajectories and the fixed loss threshold. Evaluate optimization behavior relevant to H2.
6.7 — Early-Layer Weight Displacement Compare normalized first-layer weight changes across depths. Examine the relationship between gradient attenuation and parameter movement.
6.8 — Validation Performance & Convergence Summarize training loss, validation metrics, and threshold attainment. Compare learning progress and classification performance.
6.9 — Stage A Findings & Interpretation Integrate results from Sections 6.4–6.8. Evaluate H1 and H2 under the tested conditions.

Sections 6.1–6.3 establish the experimental results and analysis-ready data.

Sections 6.4–6.8 examine gradient attenuation, trainability, and validation performance.

Section 6.9 integrates the evidence and discusses its interpretation.

4. Measurements & Analysis¶

Stage A uses the measurement definitions and logging protocol established in Part 4.

Measurement Definition / Analysis Research Role
Layer-wise RMS weight gradient RMS of layer.weight.grad for each hidden Linear layer. Quantify gradient magnitudes across network layers.
Relative gradient ratio First hidden-layer RMS divided by last hidden-layer RMS within a run. Compare relative early-layer attenuation across depths.
Gradient evolution Mean sampled RMS gradient by hidden layer and epoch. Examine changes in gradient magnitude during training.
Normalized first-layer weight displacement Frobenius norm of the difference between current and initial first-layer weights, divided by the initial weight norm. Quantify net early-layer parameter movement.
Training-loss trajectory Sample-weighted mean training CrossEntropyLoss by epoch. Assess optimization progress.
Epochs-to-threshold First epoch with mean training loss ≤ 1.50. Compare a predefined learning-progress milestone.
Validation metrics Validation loss, accuracy, and macro-F1. Assess classification performance on held-out validation data.

Statistical reporting: The main metrics are summarized using the mean and sample standard deviation across three random seeds, where applicable.

For runs that do not reach the training-loss threshold within 20 epochs, threshold attainment is reported as "Not reached" rather than assigning an arbitrary convergence epoch.

Interpretation: RMS weight-gradient attenuation is evidence about parameter-gradient magnitudes, not a direct measurement of activation Jacobians. Likewise, normalized weight displacement measures net movement from initialization, not the sum of individual SGD updates.

Associations among gradient attenuation, weight displacement, and training performance are evaluated empirically; these measurements do not independently establish causality.

5. Connection to Stage B & Final Reporting¶

The completed Stage A results provide the depth-dependent baseline for the controlled activation comparison in Part 7.

Part 7 — Stage B fixes network depth at D5 and compares Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU under the shared Xavier Uniform initialization and training protocol. The D5 Sigmoid runs from Stage A are reused as the baseline.

Part 8 — Final Analysis consolidates the completed Stage A and Stage B results, verifies experimental consistency, and presents the final interpretation of H1, H2, H3, and study limitations.

6.1 — Stage A Setup & Single-Seed Check¶

Objective: Run the main Stage A depth experiment with one random seed to verify that the training and gradient-measurement pipeline works consistently across MLPs with 2, 5, 10, and 20 hidden layers, while keeping all other experimental conditions fixed.

Procedure:

  1. Use the finalized configuration from Part 5:

    • Dataset: BloodMNIST official training and validation splits, with the same preprocessing and normalization from Part 1.
    • Models: D2, D5, D10, and D20, each with 256 neurons per hidden layer and 8 output classes.
    • Activation: Sigmoid for all hidden layers.
    • Initialization: Xavier Uniform (gain = 1), with zero biases.
    • Loss function: CrossEntropyLoss.
    • Optimizer: SGD, learning rate = 0.1, momentum = 0, weight decay = 0.
    • Training batch size = 128; full training epochs = 20.
    • Random seed = 0 (the first seed in cfg.seeds).
    • Gradient logging: First 100 global training steps, plus the first 10 batches of each epoch.
    • Training-loss threshold = 1.50 (already fixed in Part 5; used later for convergence analysis).

  2. Run the four network depths independently:

    • Reuse run_training() from Section 5.1 instead of rebuilding the model, optimizer, DataLoader, or training loop.
    • For each depth, create a fresh MLP and SGD optimizer with the same experimental settings.
    • During training (model.train()), each batch follows: forward propagation → CrossEntropyLoss → backpropagation → gradient recording → SGD parameter update.
    • After each training epoch, switch to evaluation mode (model.eval()) and calculate validation loss, accuracy, and macro-F1 without backpropagation or parameter updates.
    • Train each model for the full 20 epochs, using all training batches.

  3. Verify and store the results:

    • Confirm that each run completed 20 epochs and produced the expected gradient and first-layer weight-change records.
    • Check that the recorded losses and gradient measurements are finite.
    • Store each complete run in stage_a_runs[(depth, seed)], including the training history, early-step gradients, epoch-level gradients, and normalized first-layer weight changes.
    • Display the final training loss, validation loss, validation accuracy, and validation macro-F1 for each depth.

Purpose:

Establish a controlled comparison in which network depth is the only intentionally varied experimental factor. Using the same dataset, preprocessing, architecture width, activation, initialization rule, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epoch budget, random-seed policy, and measurement protocol helps isolate the effect of increasing depth on gradient propagation and trainability.

Running one seed first also allows the complete Stage A pipeline to be verified before expanding the experiment to additional random seeds.

Expected Results:

  • Four completed independent training runs: D2, D5, D10, and D20, each trained for 20 epochs with seed 0.
  • Each run returns:
    • run_config: Configuration used for that run.
    • history: Per-epoch training loss, validation loss, validation accuracy, and validation macro-F1.
    • step_records: Layer-wise RMS gradients recorded during the first 100 global training steps.
    • epoch_gradients: Mean RMS gradients per hidden layer and epoch, calculated from the first 10 batches of each epoch.
    • weight_changes: Cumulative normalized weight change of the first hidden layer after each epoch.
  • A dictionary named stage_a_runs containing all four results, indexed by (depth, seed).
  • Successful completion of the single-seed check, without requiring any particular model to achieve a predefined accuracy or loss value.

Role in the Experiment:

Section 6.1 begins the main Stage A controlled experiment and collects the initial evidence for:

  • H1 — Depth Effect: Determine whether increasing depth is associated with stronger gradient attenuation in earlier hidden layers.
  • H2 — Trainability Effect: Examine whether stronger early-layer gradient attenuation is associated with smaller first-layer weight changes and slower learning.

The recorded results will be reused in subsequent Stage A sections for gradient comparisons, training-loss curves, epochs-to-threshold calculations, validation-performance analysis, and the three main figures.

Unlike the short smoke test in Section 5.1 and the 3-epoch learning-rate pilot in Section 5.2, these are full-length Stage A training runs. The test split remains untouched.

stage_a_seed = cfg.seeds[0]       # Use seed 0 first; the remaining seeds are handled later.

stage_a_runs = {}                # Store each complete run as {(depth, seed): result_dict}.

# Confirm the two design choices that distinguish Stage A from later experiments.
assert cfg.activation == "sigmoid" and cfg.init == "xavier_uniform"  # Fixed activation and initialization.
assert cfg.optimizer == "sgd" and cfg.loss_threshold is not None     # Part 5 must have finalized the protocol.

print(f"Optimizer: {cfg.optimizer.upper()} | LR: {cfg.lr:g} | Momentum: {cfg.momentum:g} | Weight decay: {cfg.weight_decay:g}")
print(f"Batch size: {cfg.batch_size} | Train/validation: official BloodMNIST splits")

# Train four fresh MLPs independently using the SAME data pipeline, optimizer, and logging protocol.
for depth in stage_a_depths:                  # Loop through D2, D5, D10, and D20.
    print(f"\nTraining D{depth} (seed={stage_a_seed})...")

    result = run_training(
        depth=depth,                         # The single experimental variable: hidden-layer count.
        seed=stage_a_seed,                   # Same seed policy for model initialization and shuffling.
        activation=cfg.activation,           # Sigmoid in every hidden layer for all Stage A runs.
        lr=cfg.lr,                           # Frozen primary learning rate from Section 5.3.
        epochs=cfg.epochs,                   # Full 20 epochs; not a short pilot or smoke test.
        max_batches=None                     # Process ALL training batches in every epoch.
    )

    # Verify the returned training history and gradient/weight-change measurements.
    history = result["history"]                 # One row of train/validation metrics per completed epoch.
    epoch_gradients = result["epoch_gradients"] # One sampled mean RMS gradient per hidden layer/epoch.
    weight_changes = result["weight_changes"]  # One cumulative first-layer weight-change value per epoch.

    assert len(history) == cfg.epochs                  # All planned epochs must have finished.
    assert len(epoch_gradients) == depth * cfg.epochs  # One gradient record per hidden layer/epoch.
    assert len(weight_changes) == cfg.epochs           # One first-layer weight-change record per epoch.
    assert len(result["step_records"]) > 0             # Early-step hidden-layer gradients were also recorded.

    assert all(
        np.isfinite(row[metric])
        for row in history
        for metric in ("train_loss", "val_loss", "val_accuracy", "val_macro_f1")
    )                                                  # Training and validation metrics must be finite.

    assert all(np.isfinite(row["mean_grad_rms"]) for row in epoch_gradients)
    assert all(np.isfinite(row["first_layer_weight_change"]) for row in weight_changes)

    stage_a_runs[(depth, stage_a_seed)] = result       # Save the complete independent run for later analysis.
    last_epoch = history[-1]                          # Final training/validation metrics after epoch 20.

    print(
        f"D{depth:>2} complete | "
        f"Train loss: {last_epoch['train_loss']:.4f} | "
        f"Val loss: {last_epoch['val_loss']:.4f} | "
        f"Val acc: {last_epoch['val_accuracy']:.4f} | "
        f"Val macro-F1: {last_epoch['val_macro_f1']:.4f}"
    )

# Confirm that every requested depth has a stored result for the single-seed check.
assert len(stage_a_runs) == len(stage_a_depths)   # Four independent D2/D5/D10/D20 runs.

print(f"\nStage A single-seed check: COMPLETE ({len(stage_a_runs)} runs, seed={stage_a_seed})")

6.1 — Results, Preliminary Observations & Interpretation¶

Implementation:

  • Successfully completed four independent MLP training runs: D2, D5, D10, and D20.
  • Used the same BloodMNIST training/validation splits, hidden width (256), Sigmoid activation, Xavier Uniform initialization, CrossEntropyLoss, and SGD optimizer (LR = 0.1, momentum = 0, weight decay = 0).
  • Trained each model for 20 full epochs with random seed 0 and batch size 128.
  • Reused run_training() from Section 5.1 to perform training, validation, gradient recording, and first-layer weight-change measurements.
  • Stored all results in stage_a_runs[(depth, seed)].
  • Verified that all four runs completed the expected epochs and produced finite recorded metrics, with the expected gradient and weight-change record counts.

Results (Seed 0, Epoch 20):

Model Train Loss Val Loss Val Accuracy Val Macro-F1
D2 0.4028 0.5377 0.8020 0.7613
D5 1.2604 1.2698 0.4486 0.3133
D10 2.0116 2.0181 0.1945 0.0407
D20 2.0117 2.0192 0.1945 0.0407

Preliminary Observations:

  1. D2 achieved the strongest performance, with the lowest training/validation losses and highest validation accuracy and macro-F1.
  2. D5 showed substantially weaker performance than D2, despite using the same training configuration.
  3. D10 and D20 exhibited high training losses and very low validation performance, suggesting considerable difficulty learning under the current experimental conditions.
  4. These results reveal a strong depth-dependent performance difference for seed 0, but do not independently establish that vanishing gradients caused the observed behavior.

Interpretation & Role in the Experiment:

The single-seed results suggest that increasing MLP depth may negatively affect optimization and classification performance under the controlled Sigmoid–Xavier–SGD setup.

To investigate the underlying mechanism:

  • H1 — Gradient Propagation: Compare layer-wise RMS gradients to determine whether early hidden layers receive substantially smaller gradients as depth increases.
  • H2 — Early-Layer Trainability: Examine normalized first-layer weight changes, training-loss trajectories, and epochs-to-threshold (1.50) to assess whether gradient attenuation is associated with reduced parameter updates and slower learning.

These observations are preliminary because they represent only one random seed. Additional seeds and gradient-based analyses are required before drawing broader conclusions.

6.2 — Complete Stage A Runs (Multi-Seed Extension)¶

Objective:

Complete the Stage A network-depth experiment across three random seeds (0, 1, and 2), while reusing the four seed-0 runs from Section 6.1. Collect and preserve the training, validation, gradient, and early-layer weight-change measurements required to investigate H1 and H2.

Procedure:

  1. Reuse the finalized experimental configuration:

    • Dataset: BloodMNIST official training and validation splits, using the same normalization and preprocessing.
    • Models: D2, D5, D10, and D20, with a constant hidden width of 256 and 8 output classes.
    • Activation: Sigmoid.
    • Initialization: Xavier Uniform (gain = 1), with zero biases.
    • Loss function: CrossEntropyLoss.
    • Optimizer: SGD, learning rate = 0.1, momentum = 0, weight decay = 0.
    • Training: Batch size = 128, 20 full epochs per run.
    • Random seeds: (0, 1, 2).
    • Gradient logging: First 100 global training steps and the first 10 batches of each epoch.
    • Training-loss threshold: 1.50, finalized in Part 5.

  2. Complete the missing depth–seed combinations:

    • Reuse stage_a_runs from Section 6.1, which already contains the four completed seed-0 runs.
    • Iterate over D2, D5, D10, and D20, using seeds 1 and 2.
    • Skip any run already present in stage_a_runs to avoid unnecessary retraining.
    • Call the existing run_training() function for each missing combination. Each call creates a fresh MLP, optimizer, and gradient recorder.
    • During training, each batch follows: forward propagation → CrossEntropyLoss → backpropagation → gradient recording → SGD parameter update.
    • After every epoch, evaluate the model on the validation split without gradient computation or parameter updates.

  3. Verify and store each completed run:

    • Confirm that every newly completed run contains 20 epoch-history records.
    • Check the expected number of early-step gradient records, epoch-level gradient records, and first-layer weight-change records.
    • Verify that the recorded training/validation metrics and gradient measurements are finite.
    • Store each run in the existing stage_a_runs[(depth, seed)] dictionary.
    • Save the accumulated results to results/stage_a/stage_a_runs.pt after each new run, reducing the risk of losing completed experiments if later runs are interrupted.

  4. Review the complete Stage A results:

    • Confirm that the dictionary contains all 12 depth–seed combinations.
    • Display the final training loss, validation loss, validation accuracy, and validation macro-F1 for each run.
    • Calculate the first epoch at which mean training loss reaches the predefined threshold of 1.50; report "Not reached" when the threshold is not reached within 20 epochs.
    • Keep the individual seed results separate. Mean and standard deviation across seeds will be calculated in Section 6.3.

Purpose:

Investigate whether the depth-dependent differences observed with seed 0 in Section 6.1 remain consistent under different random initializations and training-data shuffles.

Using the same seed set and training protocol across all network depths supports a controlled comparison while accounting for variation caused by randomness.

Expected Results:

  • A total of 12 independent Stage A runs: 4 depths × 3 seeds.
  • Four previously completed seed-0 runs are reused, and eight additional runs are completed.
  • Each run contains:
    • run_config: Configuration used for that run.
    • history: Per-epoch training loss, validation loss, validation accuracy, and validation macro-F1.
    • step_records: Layer-wise RMS gradients from the first 100 global training steps.
    • epoch_gradients: Mean RMS gradients for each hidden layer and epoch, based on the first 10 training batches of each epoch.
    • weight_changes: Cumulative normalized first-hidden-layer weight change after each epoch.
  • A complete stage_a_runs dictionary containing all 12 runs.
  • A saved checkpoint containing the accumulated raw experimental results.
  • Per-run epochs-to-threshold values based on the fixed threshold of 1.50.

No specific loss, accuracy, or gradient magnitude is required for a run to be considered valid, provided the experiment completes and the recorded measurements are numerically valid.

Role in the Experiment:

Section 6.2 completes the data-collection stage for the main network-depth comparison.

  • H1 — Depth Effect: The recorded layer-wise RMS gradients will be used to examine how gradient propagation changes as MLP depth increases.
  • H2 — Trainability Effect: The recorded first-layer weight changes, training-loss trajectories, and epochs-to-threshold will be used to investigate whether stronger gradient attenuation is associated with reduced early-layer trainability and slower learning.

Section 6.3 will organize the recorded measurements into analysis-ready tables and calculate mean ± standard deviation across the three seeds. Subsequent sections will generate Figures 1–3 and interpret the evidence for H1 and H2.

The BloodMNIST test split remains untouched. Since the three-seed Stage A experiment is completed here, Part 8 will reuse these runs for final multi-seed analysis rather than retraining them.

# Reuse the four seed-0 results from Section 6.1 and prepare a checkpoint for Stage A.
assert all((depth, cfg.seeds[0]) in stage_a_runs for depth in cfg.depths), (
    "Run Section 6.1 first: the four seed-0 results must already exist."
)

stage_a_path = Path(cfg.results_dir) / "stage_a" / "stage_a_runs.pt"  # File containing all completed Stage A runs
stage_a_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)              # Create results/stage_a if it does not exist

torch.save(stage_a_runs, stage_a_path)       # Preserve the existing seed-0 runs before starting new training

print("=== Section 6.2 — Complete Stage A Runs ===")
print(f"Depths: {cfg.depths} | Seeds: {cfg.seeds} | Epochs: {cfg.epochs}")
print(f"Activation: {cfg.activation} | Initialization: {cfg.init}")
print(f"Optimizer: {cfg.optimizer.upper()} | LR: {cfg.lr:g} | Loss threshold: {cfg.loss_threshold:.2f}")
print(f"Runs already completed: {len(stage_a_runs)}")
print(f"Total planned runs: {len(cfg.depths) * len(cfg.seeds)}")

# Run every missing depth-seed combination using the same training and measurement pipeline.
for depth in cfg.depths:                     # Compare D2, D5, D10, and D20 with all other settings fixed.
    for seed in cfg.seeds:                   # Repeat each depth using seeds 0, 1, and 2.

        run_key = (depth, seed)               # Unique dictionary key identifying one independent run.

        if run_key in stage_a_runs:
            print(f"\nD{depth:>2} | Seed {seed}: Already completed — reusing results.")
            continue                         # Skip seed-0 runs and any other run already completed.

        print(f"\nTraining D{depth} | Seed {seed}...")

        result = run_training(
            depth=depth,                     # Number of hidden layers; the independent variable in Stage A.
            seed=seed,                       # Controls initialization and training-data shuffling.
            activation=cfg.activation,       # Keep Sigmoid fixed across all depths and seeds.
            lr=cfg.lr,                       # Reuse the learning rate frozen in Section 5.3.
            epochs=cfg.epochs,               # Train for the same full 20-epoch budget.
            max_batches=None                 # Use every training batch, not a shortened pilot.
        )

        # Check the measurements returned by the existing training and gradient-recording functions.
        history = result["history"]                  # Training and validation metrics for each epoch.
        step_records = result["step_records"]        # Hidden-layer gradient RMS for the first 100 training steps.
        epoch_gradients = result["epoch_gradients"]  # Hidden-layer mean RMS gradient for every epoch.
        weight_changes = result["weight_changes"]   # First-layer cumulative normalized weight change per epoch.

        assert len(history) == cfg.epochs                  # One training/validation record per epoch.
        assert len(step_records) == 100 * depth            # First 100 global steps × number of hidden layers.
        assert len(epoch_gradients) == cfg.epochs * depth  # One mean gradient per hidden layer and epoch.
        assert len(weight_changes) == cfg.epochs           # One first-layer weight-change record per epoch.

        assert all(
            np.isfinite(row[metric])
            for row in history
            for metric in ("train_loss", "val_loss", "val_accuracy", "val_macro_f1")
        ), f"Non-finite training/validation metric detected for D{depth}, seed {seed}"

        assert all(np.isfinite(row["grad_rms"]) for row in step_records)
        assert all(np.isfinite(row["mean_grad_rms"]) for row in epoch_gradients)
        assert all(np.isfinite(row["first_layer_weight_change"]) for row in weight_changes)

        # Save only completed, verified runs; keep the original results for later analysis.
        stage_a_runs[run_key] = result                 # Add the complete result dictionary without modifying its metrics.
        torch.save(stage_a_runs, stage_a_path)        # Save progress after each run instead of waiting for all runs.

        last_epoch = history[-1]                      # Retrieve the final metrics after 20 training epochs.

        print(
            f"D{depth:>2} | Seed {seed} complete | "
            f"Train loss: {last_epoch['train_loss']:.4f} | "
            f"Val loss: {last_epoch['val_loss']:.4f} | "
            f"Val acc: {last_epoch['val_accuracy']:.4f} | "
            f"Val macro-F1: {last_epoch['val_macro_f1']:.4f}"
        )

# Verify that the complete Stage A experiment contains every required depth-seed combination.
expected_runs = {(depth, seed) for depth in cfg.depths for seed in cfg.seeds}  # All 4 × 3 combinations
assert set(stage_a_runs) == expected_runs, "Stage A is missing one or more depth-seed runs."

print("\n=== Stage A — Final Results for All Runs ===")
print(f"{'Model':<8} {'Seed':<6} {'Train Loss':<12} {'Val Loss':<12} {'Val Acc':<12} {'Macro-F1':<12} {'Threshold'}")

# Display the final metrics and the first epoch reaching the fixed training-loss threshold.
for depth in cfg.depths:
    for seed in cfg.seeds:

        history = stage_a_runs[(depth, seed)]["history"]    # Retrieve the 20-epoch history for this run.
        final = history[-1]                                # Last epoch's training and validation metrics.

        reached_epoch = next(
            (
                epoch for epoch, row in enumerate(history, start=1)
                if row["train_loss"] <= cfg.loss_threshold  # First epoch with mean train loss <= 1.50
            ),
            None                                          # No epoch reached the threshold within 20 epochs.
        )

        threshold_status = reached_epoch if reached_epoch is not None else "Not reached"

        print(
            f"D{depth:<7} {seed:<6} "
            f"{final['train_loss']:<12.4f} "
            f"{final['val_loss']:<12.4f} "
            f"{final['val_accuracy']:<12.4f} "
            f"{final['val_macro_f1']:<12.4f} "
            f"{threshold_status}"
        )

print(f"\nStage A: COMPLETE ({len(stage_a_runs)} runs across {len(cfg.seeds)} seeds)")
print(f"Results saved to: {stage_a_path}")
print("Ready for Section 6.3 — Organize Stage A Results.")

6.2 — Results, Preliminary Observations & Interpretation¶

Implementation:

  • Successfully completed 12 independent Stage A training runs (4 network depths × 3 random seeds).
  • Reused the four completed seed-0 runs from Section 6.1 and trained the eight remaining depth–seed combinations.
  • Used the same controlled experimental configuration across all runs:
    • Dataset: BloodMNIST official training and validation splits.
    • Models: D2, D5, D10, and D20; hidden width = 256.
    • Activation: Sigmoid; initialization: Xavier Uniform.
    • Loss: CrossEntropyLoss; optimizer: SGD, LR = 0.1, momentum = 0, weight decay = 0.
    • Training: 20 full epochs per run, batch size = 128.
    • Random seeds: 0, 1, and 2.
  • Reused run_training() to perform training, validation, gradient recording, and first-layer weight-change measurements.
  • Verified the expected number of epoch histories, gradient records, and weight-change records, along with the numerical validity of the checked measurements.
  • Stored the complete experimental results in stage_a_runs[(depth, seed)] and saved them to results/stage_a/stage_a_runs.pt.
  • Calculated and displayed epochs-to-threshold using the predefined training-loss threshold of 1.50.

Results (Epoch 20 — Values Visible in the Recorded Outputs):

Note: All 12 runs completed successfully.

Preliminary Observations:

  1. D2 consistently achieved stronger classification performance across all three seeds, with validation accuracy ranging from 80.20% to 82.42%.
  2. D5 showed substantially weaker performance, with validation accuracy ranging from 44.86% to 48.71%.
  3. The performance difference between D2 and D5 was consistent across the three observed seeds, suggesting a strong depth-dependent difference under the fixed Sigmoid–Xavier–SGD configuration.
  4. These classification results alone cannot establish vanishing gradients as the cause. Layer-wise RMS gradients, normalized first-layer weight changes, and training-loss trajectories must also be examined.
  5. The complete D10/D20 measurements and variability across seeds will be analyzed in subsequent sections.

Interpretation & Role in the Experiment:

The experiment has completed its main Stage A data collection, providing the measurements required to investigate:

  • H1 — Depth Effect: Whether deeper MLPs exhibit stronger gradient attenuation in earlier hidden layers.
  • H2 — Trainability Effect: Whether smaller early-layer gradients are associated with smaller normalized weight changes and slower training-loss reduction.

Using three random seeds helps assess whether the observed depth-dependent patterns are consistent across different model initializations and training-data shuffles.

Connection to the Next Section:

Section 6.3 will reuse stage_a_runs without retraining any models. It will organize the recorded measurements into DataFrames, calculate mean ± standard deviation across seeds, and prepare the data for gradient visualizations, convergence analysis, and the Stage A results table.

6.3 — Organize Stage A Results¶

Objective:

Organize the measurements collected from the 12 completed Stage A runs into analysis-ready Pandas DataFrames. Calculate epochs-to-threshold for each independent run and summarize the main experimental metrics across three random seeds using mean and standard deviation.

Procedure:

  1. Reuse the completed Stage A results:

    • Read stage_a_runs from Section 6.2, containing four network depths (D2, D5, D10, D20) and three random seeds (0, 1, 2).
    • Verify that all 12 depth–seed combinations are present.
    • Reuse the recorded measurements without creating or retraining any models.

  2. Organize the raw measurements into DataFrames:

    • stage_a_history_df: Training loss, validation loss, validation accuracy, and validation macro-F1 for each depth, seed, and epoch.
    • stage_a_gradients_df: Layer-wise mean RMS weight gradients for each depth, seed, hidden layer, and epoch. Each epoch-level value is the arithmetic mean of gradient RMS measurements from the first 10 training batches of that epoch.
    • stage_a_weights_df: Cumulative normalized weight change of Hidden Layer 1 after each epoch, relative to its initial weights.

    Preserve the depth, seed, epoch, and layer identifiers so measurements can be compared without mixing different runs or hidden layers.

  3. Calculate one summary for each independent run:

    • Extract the final training loss, validation loss, validation accuracy, and validation macro-F1 after epoch 20.
    • Extract the mean RMS gradients of Hidden Layer 1 and the last hidden layer during epoch 1.
    • Extract the final cumulative normalized weight change of Hidden Layer 1 after epoch 20.
    • Calculate epochs-to-threshold using the predefined training-loss threshold of 1.50.
    • Record the first epoch with mean training loss ≤ 1.50. If the threshold is not reached within 20 epochs, record a missing value (NaN).

    Store the results in stage_a_run_summary_df, containing one row per depth–seed combination.

  4. Aggregate results across three random seeds:

    • Group the per-run summaries by network depth.
    • Calculate mean and sample standard deviation (ddof = 1) for final training/validation metrics, selected gradient measurements, and final first-layer weight changes.
    • Count how many seeds reached the predefined training-loss threshold.
    • Calculate the mean and standard deviation of epochs-to-threshold only among runs that reached the threshold, while reporting the number of successful runs separately.

    Store the results in stage_a_summary_df, containing one row per network depth.

  5. Verify and save the organized results:

    • Confirm the expected number of records in each DataFrame.
    • Verify that all epoch-level gradient means were calculated from 10 sampled training batches.
    • Save the per-run and depth-level summary tables as CSV files.
    • Display the aggregated validation metrics and epochs-to-threshold results.

Purpose:

Convert the raw experimental measurements from Section 6.2 into a consistent and reproducible format for comparing network depths.

Keeping individual seed results separate before aggregation preserves information about run-to-run variability. Reporting mean ± standard deviation helps assess whether the observed depth-dependent behavior is consistent across random seeds.

Expected Results:

DataFrame Expected Rows Description
stage_a_history_df 240 12 runs × 20 epochs
stage_a_gradients_df 2,220 3 seeds × 20 epochs × 37 hidden layers across D2/D5/D10/D20
stage_a_weights_df 240 One first-layer weight-change record per run and epoch
stage_a_run_summary_df 12 One summary per independent run
stage_a_summary_df 4 One aggregated summary per depth

The original stage_a_runs dictionary remains unchanged, including the first-100-step gradient records, which are retained for later analysis if needed.

Role in the Experiment:

Section 6.3 prepares the measurements required to investigate:

  • H1 — Depth Effect: Whether deeper MLPs exhibit stronger gradient attenuation in earlier hidden layers, based on layer-wise RMS gradients.
  • H2 — Trainability Effect: Whether smaller early-layer gradients are associated with smaller cumulative first-layer weight changes and slower training-loss reduction.

The resulting DataFrames will be reused in:

  • Section 6.4: Figure 1 — Gradient Magnitude vs. Layer.
  • Section 6.5: Figure 2 — Gradient Evolution During Training.
  • Section 6.6: Figure 3 — Training Loss Curves.
  • Section 6.7: Early-Layer Weight Change Analysis.
  • Sections 6.8–6.9: Validation performance, convergence analysis, and interpretation of H1/H2.

No new training, validation, gradient computation, or model-parameter updates are performed. The BloodMNIST test split remains untouched.

# Verify that Section 6.2 has completed all 12 Stage A runs before processing their results.
expected_runs = {(depth, seed) for depth in cfg.depths for seed in cfg.seeds}  # All 4 depths × 3 seeds

assert set(stage_a_runs) == expected_runs, "Stage A must contain all 12 depth-seed runs."
assert cfg.loss_threshold is not None, "The training-loss threshold must be finalized in Part 5."

# Prepare lists to collect measurements from the existing Stage A result dictionaries.
history_rows = []        # Per-epoch training and validation metrics
gradient_rows = []       # Per-epoch RMS gradients for each hidden layer
weight_rows = []         # Per-epoch cumulative first-layer weight changes
run_summary_rows = []    # Final metrics and convergence information for each run


# Extract the recorded measurements from each independently trained MLP.
for (depth, seed), result in sorted(stage_a_runs.items()):

    history = result["history"]                   # List of 20 dictionaries containing training/validation metrics
    gradients = result["epoch_gradients"]          # Mean RMS gradients for each hidden layer and epoch
    weight_changes = result["weight_changes"]     # Cumulative first-layer weight changes after each epoch

    # Organize the training and validation history, keeping each run and epoch identifiable.
    for epoch, row in enumerate(history, start=1):

        history_rows.append({
            "depth": depth,                       # Number of hidden layers in this MLP
            "seed": seed,                         # Random seed used to initialize and train this model
            "epoch": epoch,                       # Epoch number, starting at 1
            "train_loss": row["train_loss"],       # Mean CrossEntropyLoss over the training split
            "val_loss": row["val_loss"],           # Mean CrossEntropyLoss over the validation split
            "val_accuracy": row["val_accuracy"],   # Correct predictions / total validation images
            "val_macro_f1": row["val_macro_f1"]    # Arithmetic mean of the 8 class-wise F1 scores
        })

    # Organize layer-wise gradient RMS measurements recorded during training.
    for row in gradients:

        gradient_rows.append({
            "depth": depth,                       # MLP depth to which this gradient measurement belongs
            "seed": seed,                         # Random seed for this run
            "epoch": row["epoch"],                # Epoch when the gradient was measured
            "layer": row["layer"],                # Hidden-layer index: 1 is closest to the input
            "mean_grad_rms": row["mean_grad_rms"], # Average RMS weight gradient over sampled batches
            "batches": row["batches"]             # Number of batches contributing to the mean (10)
        })

    # Organize cumulative first-layer weight changes relative to the initial weights.
    for row in weight_changes:

        weight_rows.append({
            "depth": depth,                       # MLP depth being evaluated
            "seed": seed,                         # Random seed for this model
            "epoch": row["epoch"],                # Epoch after which the weights were measured
            "first_layer_weight_change": row["first_layer_weight_change"]  # ||W1(t)-W1(0)|| / ||W1(0)||
        })

    # Find the first epoch when the mean training loss reaches the predefined threshold.
    reached_epoch = next(
        (
            epoch for epoch, row in enumerate(history, start=1)
            if row["train_loss"] <= cfg.loss_threshold  # First epoch with training loss <= 1.50
        ),
        None                                          # None = threshold not reached within 20 epochs
    )

    # Extract representative early-training gradients from the first 10 batches of epoch 1.
    first_grad = next(
        row["mean_grad_rms"] for row in gradients
        if row["epoch"] == 1 and row["layer"] == 1     # RMS gradient of the first hidden layer
    )

    last_grad = next(
        row["mean_grad_rms"] for row in gradients
        if row["epoch"] == 1 and row["layer"] == depth # RMS gradient of the last hidden layer
    )

    # Summarize final classification performance and trainability measurements for this run.
    final = history[-1]                              # Final training/validation metrics after epoch 20

    run_summary_rows.append({
        "depth": depth,
        "seed": seed,
        "train_loss": final["train_loss"],            # Final mean training loss
        "val_loss": final["val_loss"],                # Final mean validation loss
        "val_accuracy": final["val_accuracy"],        # Final validation accuracy
        "val_macro_f1": final["val_macro_f1"],        # Final validation macro-F1
        "grad_rms_l1_epoch1": first_grad,             # Early gradient magnitude at Hidden Layer 1
        "grad_rms_last_epoch1": last_grad,            # Early gradient magnitude at the last hidden layer
        "weight_change_l1_final": weight_changes[-1]["first_layer_weight_change"],  # Final relative W1 change
        "epochs_to_threshold": reached_epoch          # First epoch reaching loss <= 1.50, or missing
    })


# Convert the collected measurements into analysis-ready Pandas DataFrames.
stage_a_history_df = pd.DataFrame(history_rows)             # One row per depth, seed, and epoch
stage_a_gradients_df = pd.DataFrame(gradient_rows)           # One row per depth, seed, epoch, and hidden layer
stage_a_weights_df = pd.DataFrame(weight_rows)               # One first-layer weight-change record per epoch
stage_a_run_summary_df = pd.DataFrame(run_summary_rows)     # One summary row per independent run

# Verify the expected number of records and the fixed gradient-logging protocol.
assert len(stage_a_history_df) == len(cfg.depths) * len(cfg.seeds) * cfg.epochs
assert len(stage_a_gradients_df) == sum(cfg.depths) * len(cfg.seeds) * cfg.epochs
assert len(stage_a_weights_df) == len(stage_a_history_df)
assert len(stage_a_run_summary_df) == len(expected_runs)
assert (stage_a_gradients_df["batches"] == 10).all()         # Every epoch-level gradient mean uses 10 batches


# Aggregate the final measurements across seeds within each network depth.
stage_a_summary_df = (
    stage_a_run_summary_df.groupby("depth", as_index=False)  # Combine three independent seeds per depth
    .agg(
        n_seeds=("seed", "nunique"),                         # Number of random seeds for each depth

        train_loss_mean=("train_loss", "mean"),              # Mean final training loss
        train_loss_std=("train_loss", "std"),                # Sample standard deviation across seeds

        val_loss_mean=("val_loss", "mean"),                  # Mean final validation loss
        val_loss_std=("val_loss", "std"),                    # Sample standard deviation of validation loss

        val_accuracy_mean=("val_accuracy", "mean"),          # Mean final validation accuracy
        val_accuracy_std=("val_accuracy", "std"),            # Variation in accuracy across seeds

        val_macro_f1_mean=("val_macro_f1", "mean"),          # Mean final validation macro-F1
        val_macro_f1_std=("val_macro_f1", "std"),            # Variation in macro-F1 across seeds

        grad_rms_l1_epoch1_mean=("grad_rms_l1_epoch1", "mean"),    # Mean early gradient at Hidden Layer 1
        grad_rms_l1_epoch1_std=("grad_rms_l1_epoch1", "std"),      # Gradient variation across seeds

        grad_rms_last_epoch1_mean=("grad_rms_last_epoch1", "mean"),  # Mean early gradient at last hidden layer
        grad_rms_last_epoch1_std=("grad_rms_last_epoch1", "std"),    # Gradient variation across seeds

        weight_change_l1_final_mean=("weight_change_l1_final", "mean"),  # Mean cumulative W1 change
        weight_change_l1_final_std=("weight_change_l1_final", "std"),    # Variation in W1 change

        seeds_reached_threshold=("epochs_to_threshold", "count"), # Count runs reaching the loss threshold
        epochs_to_threshold_mean=("epochs_to_threshold", "mean"),  # Mean among runs reaching threshold
        epochs_to_threshold_std=("epochs_to_threshold", "std")     # Sample std among runs reaching threshold
    )
)


# Save the compact summary tables; all raw measurements remain available in stage_a_runs.
stage_a_output_dir = Path(cfg.results_dir) / "stage_a"     # Same results folder used in Section 6.2
stage_a_output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)     # Ensure the folder exists

stage_a_run_summary_df.to_csv(
    stage_a_output_dir / "stage_a_run_summary.csv", index=False  # Save per-run metrics without row indices
)

stage_a_summary_df.to_csv(
    stage_a_output_dir / "stage_a_summary.csv", index=False      # Save aggregated mean/std statistics
)


# Display the record counts to confirm that all Stage A measurements are organized.
print("=== Section 6.3 — Organized Stage A Results ===")
print(f"Training/validation history: {len(stage_a_history_df)} rows")
print(f"Layer-wise RMS gradients: {len(stage_a_gradients_df)} rows")
print(f"First-layer weight changes: {len(stage_a_weights_df)} rows")
print(f"Per-run summaries: {len(stage_a_run_summary_df)} rows")
print(f"Depth-level summaries: {len(stage_a_summary_df)} rows")


# Review final validation performance aggregated across the three random seeds.
print("\n=== Final Validation Performance — Mean ± Std Across Seeds ===")

display(
    stage_a_summary_df[[
        "depth", "n_seeds",
        "val_accuracy_mean", "val_accuracy_std",
        "val_macro_f1_mean", "val_macro_f1_std",
        "seeds_reached_threshold"
    ]].round(4)
)


# Review when each independent run first reached the training-loss threshold.
print(f"\n=== Epochs-to-Threshold (Training Loss <= {cfg.loss_threshold:.2f}) ===")

print(
    stage_a_run_summary_df[["depth", "seed", "epochs_to_threshold"]]
    .to_string(index=False, na_rep="Not reached")  # Missing values represent runs that never reached the threshold
)

print("\nSection 6.3 completed — Stage A results are ready for analysis.")

6.3 — Results, Preliminary Observations & Interpretation¶

Implementation:

  • Successfully organized the measurements from all 12 completed Stage A runs (4 depths × 3 random seeds) without retraining any models.
  • Reused stage_a_runs from Section 6.2 and created five Pandas DataFrames:
    • stage_a_history_df: 240 records of training/validation metrics.
    • stage_a_gradients_df: 2,220 layer-wise epoch-level RMS gradient records.
    • stage_a_weights_df: 240 cumulative first-layer weight-change records.
    • stage_a_run_summary_df: 12 per-run summaries.
    • stage_a_summary_df: 4 depth-level summaries aggregated across seeds.
  • Calculated final classification metrics and selected gradient/weight-change measurements for each independent run.
  • Calculated epochs-to-threshold using the predefined mean training-loss threshold of 1.50.
  • Aggregated metrics across three seeds using mean and sample standard deviation.
  • Verified the expected record counts and the 10-batch epoch-level gradient sampling protocol.
  • Saved the per-run and depth-level summary tables as CSV files. The original raw measurements remain preserved in stage_a_runs.

Results — Final Validation Performance (Mean ± Std, 3 Seeds):

Model Val Accuracy Val Macro-F1 Seeds Reaching Loss ≤ 1.50
D2 0.8123 ± 0.0112 0.7851 ± 0.0208 3/3
D5 0.4663 ± 0.0195 0.3377 ± 0.0213 3/3
D10 0.1820 ± 0.0126 0.0385 ± 0.0022 0/3
D20 0.1820 ± 0.0126 0.0385 ± 0.0022 0/3

Results — Epochs-to-Threshold (Training Loss ≤ 1.50):

Model Seed 0 Seed 1 Seed 2 Mean ± Std (Reached Runs)
D2 2 2 2 2.00 ± 0.00
D5 15 15 14 14.67 ± 0.58
D10 Not reached Not reached Not reached N/A
D20 Not reached Not reached Not reached N/A

Note: "Not reached" means the model did not achieve the predefined training-loss threshold within the 20-epoch budget. It does not mean training failed or that the model could never reach the threshold with additional training.

Preliminary Observations:

  1. D2 showed the strongest classification performance, achieving 81.23% mean validation accuracy and 0.7851 mean validation macro-F1 across three seeds.
  2. D5 performed substantially worse than D2, with 46.63% mean validation accuracy and 0.3377 mean validation macro-F1.
  3. D10 and D20 showed very low classification performance, with identical reported aggregate validation accuracy (18.20%) and macro-F1 (0.0385). Their prediction distributions have not yet been examined.
  4. Training-loss reduction became considerably slower with depth:
    • D2 reached the threshold at epoch 2 for all three seeds.
    • D5 reached the threshold at epochs 14–15.
    • D10 and D20 did not reach the threshold within 20 epochs for any seed.
  5. The depth-dependent performance and convergence patterns were consistent across the three seeds. However, these results alone do not establish vanishing gradients as the cause.

Interpretation & Role in the Experiment:

The aggregated results show a substantial deterioration in training-loss reduction and validation performance as MLP depth increases under the fixed Sigmoid–Xavier–SGD configuration.

These observations provide preliminary evidence of depth-dependent optimization difficulties and motivate further investigation of:

  • H1 — Depth Effect: Whether early hidden layers receive substantially smaller RMS gradients in deeper networks.
  • H2 — Trainability Effect: Whether smaller early-layer gradients are associated with reduced normalized weight changes and slower training-loss reduction.

The gradient and weight-change measurements have been organized but are not yet interpreted in this section. Therefore, the relationship between gradient attenuation and the observed optimization difficulties remains to be established.

Connection to Subsequent Sections:

  • Section 6.4: Compare gradient RMS across hidden layers to investigate H1.
  • Section 6.5: Examine how layer-wise gradients evolve throughout training.
  • Section 6.6: Visualize training-loss trajectories and the predefined threshold.
  • Section 6.7: Analyze normalized first-layer weight changes.
  • Sections 6.8–6.9: Integrate the measurements, evaluate H1/H2, and discuss limitations.

6.4 — Figure 1: Gradient Magnitude vs. Layer¶

Objective:

Visualize and compare layer-wise RMS weight gradients across D2, D5, D10, and D20 to investigate whether increasing MLP depth is associated with stronger gradient attenuation in earlier hidden layers.

Procedure:

  1. Reuse the recorded gradient measurements:

    • Read stage_a_gradients_df from Section 6.3.
    • Select epoch 1 for all four network depths and three random seeds.
    • Each recorded value, mean_grad_rms, is the arithmetic mean of the RMS weight gradients measured over the first 10 training batches of epoch 1.
    • Include only hidden Linear layers, indexed from 1 (closest to the input) to depth (last hidden layer). The output layer and bias gradients are excluded.
    • Reuse the existing measurements without retraining models or recomputing gradients through backpropagation.

  2. Calculate the absolute layer-wise RMS gradients — Panel (a):

    • Group the measurements by network depth and hidden-layer index.
    • Calculate the mean and sample standard deviation across three seeds.
    • Plot the mean RMS gradient against hidden-layer index for D2, D5, D10, and D20.
    • Use a logarithmic y-axis because gradient magnitudes may differ by several orders of magnitude.
    • Show mean ± 1 standard deviation where the corresponding bounds are positive.

  3. Calculate relative RMS gradients — Panel (b):

    • For each independent depth–seed run, use the RMS gradient of its last hidden layer as the reference.
    • Calculate:

    $$ R_{d,s,l} = \frac{G_{d,s,l}}{G_{d,s,d}} $$

    where:

    • $d$: Number of hidden layers (network depth).

    • $s$: Random seed.

    • $l$: Hidden-layer index.

    • $G_{d,s,l}$: Mean RMS gradient of hidden layer $l$ during the first 10 batches of epoch 1.

    • $G_{d,s,d}$: Mean RMS gradient of the last hidden layer in the same run.

    • Calculate each ratio within its own depth–seed run before aggregating across seeds.

    • Group the resulting ratios by depth and hidden-layer index, then calculate mean ± sample standard deviation across seeds.

    • A ratio below 1 indicates a smaller RMS gradient than the last hidden layer. A ratio much smaller than 1 indicates stronger relative gradient attenuation.

    • The last hidden layer has a ratio of 1 by definition, provided its reference gradient is nonzero.

  4. Create and save Figure 1:

    • Panel (a): Absolute RMS Gradient vs. Hidden-Layer Index.
    • Panel (b): Relative RMS Gradient vs. Hidden-Layer Index.
    • Plot one curve per network depth, using consistent colors across both panels.
    • Use logarithmic y-axes and shaded bands representing mean ± 1 standard deviation.
    • Save the complete figure in PNG and PDF formats under results/stage_a/.

Purpose:

Investigate how gradient magnitudes vary along the hidden layers of networks with different depths.

Absolute RMS gradients show the scale of gradients reaching each layer, while relative RMS gradients help distinguish differences in overall gradient magnitude from attenuation between early and later hidden layers.

Using the same epoch, gradient-sampling protocol, activation function, initialization rule, optimizer, learning rate, and random-seed set supports a controlled comparison.

Expected Results:

  • One Figure 1 containing two complementary panels.
  • Four depth-specific curves (D2, D5, D10, D20) in each panel.
  • Mean ± standard deviation across three random seeds.
  • Logarithmic y-axes to display potentially very small gradients.
  • A summary table reporting first-layer absolute and relative RMS gradients for each network depth.
  • Saved files:
    • figure1_gradient_vs_layer.png
    • figure1_gradient_vs_layer.pdf

No particular gradient pattern is assumed before inspecting the actual results. Exact-zero RMS gradients cannot be displayed directly on logarithmic axes and will be omitted from the plotted curves without changing the recorded data.

Role in the Experiment:

Figure 1 provides direct gradient-based evidence for evaluating:

  • H1 — Depth Effect: Whether increasing network depth is associated with smaller gradients in earlier hidden layers, especially relative to later hidden layers.

These gradient measurements will be interpreted together with:

  • Section 6.5: Gradient evolution over training, to examine whether attenuation persists or changes across epochs.
  • Section 6.6: Training-loss trajectories, to compare learning behavior.
  • Section 6.7: Cumulative normalized first-layer weight changes, to investigate early-layer trainability.
  • Sections 6.8–6.9: Combined evidence and interpretation of H1/H2.

Interpretation Notes:

  • Epoch 1 represents early training, not the exact untrained initialization state; optimizer updates occur during the sampled batches.
  • Gradient attenuation should be evaluated from the actual layer-wise measurements, not inferred from classification accuracy alone.
  • Relative gradients quantify attenuation compared with the last hidden layer, but they do not independently establish the causal mechanism of training failure.
  • Mean ± standard deviation across three seeds describes observed variability; it does not establish statistical significance.
  • The BloodMNIST test split remains untouched.
